[2026-04-30] ## Sapiens2 pose gains traction as best 2D pose estimator

**Kijai** said Sapiens2 pose feels like the current best 2D pose estimator, with **djbfilmz** and others in the chat also praising its quality. **djbfilmz** shared Wan Animate reskinning/mo-capping-from-real-footage results, saying Sapiens2 came closest to achieving the correct pose and position: https://discord.com/channels/1076117621407223829/1145677539738665020/1499066389757952040
---
[2026-04-25] • **Kijai** tested it with extreme head movement. The face tracking doesn't keep up perfectly but shows promise for closeups. A separate face signal like WanAnimate would be needed for proper far-distance tracking, but with audio-driven lipsync and expressions already working, it's less critical: https://discord.com/channels/1076117621407223829/1457981700817817620/1497310913395691560

[2026-03-29] ## Wan Animate Artifacting Discussion

**djbfilmz** reported artifacting issues with the native Wan Animate node at high frame counts (over 165 frames), while the wrapper version handled the same shots without problems. **Kijai** said the wrapper does the looping generation automatically, which may be related to why it behaves differently. **Kijai** is developing a loop helper node to enable single-node workflows instead of multiple InfiniteTalk nodes: https://discord.com/channels/1076117621407223829/1342763350815277067/1487598565525160159

SKILL.md
---
name: reigh-debug
description: >
  Debugging router for the Reigh production stack (reigh-app frontend +
  edge functions, reigh-worker GPU workers, reigh-worker-orchestrator on
  Railway). Use when the user asks why a task failed, why a worker was
  killed, why a pipeline stalled, why the queue is backed up, why a
  generation didn't appear, or any "what's going on with prod" question
  about Reigh. Routes to the right repo, debug CLI, and log source, with
  decision tables, system_logs guidance, blast-radius, and gotchas.
---

# reigh-debug

When something breaks in the Reigh stack, start here. Routes you to the right repo, tool, and log.

If `$ARGUMENTS` (or the user prompt) is empty, run `./debug status` from the workspace root to show current state, then ask what to investigate.

> **Working directory:** All commands assume you're in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace` (or a subdir of it). If invoked from elsewhere, `cd` there first or prepend the absolute path.

---

## Repo Map

```
reigh-workspace/
  reigh-app/                  Frontend (React/Vite) + Supabase edge functions + main debug CLI
  reigh-worker/               GPU worker (Python, runs on RunPod pods)
  reigh-worker-orchestrator/  Worker scaling + API task dispatch (runs on Railway)
```

---

## Quick Start

```bash
# From the workspace root:
./debug why <task_id>              # Why did this task fail? (error + pipeline + worker)
./debug why <id1> <id2>            # Investigate multiple tasks at once
./debug status                     # What's happening? (workers, queue, failures)
./debug kill <worker_id>           # Kill a stuck/old worker
./debug reset <task_id>            # Reset a task to Queued
```

For deeper investigation, use the per-repo tools:
1. **Full task timeline** — `cd reigh-app && python scripts/debug.py task <task_id>`
2. **Pipeline tree + health** — `cd reigh-app && python scripts/debug.py pipeline <task_id>`
3. **Why was a worker killed** — `cd reigh-app && python scripts/debug.py why-killed <worker_id>`
4. **Scaling decisions** — `cd reigh-app && python scripts/debug.py scaling-audit --hours 6`
5. **System health** — `cd reigh-worker-orchestrator && python scripts/debug.py health`
```

> AGENT

Skill written. Now the actual Wan Animate best-practices, drawn from those Banodoco searches:

## Wan Animate — best practices (per Banodoco, ~last 2 months)

### Which node/workflow to use

- **Kijai's WanVideoWrapper is the default starting point.** It does looping automatically and handles long shots better than the native ComfyUI node — *djbfilmz* hit artifacting on the native node above ~165 frames; the wrapper handled the same shot fine.
- **Native is catching up:** *Ablejones* merged WanAnimate context-windows support into ComfyUI core ([PR #12645](https://github.com/Comfy-Org/ComfyUI/pull/12645)), with a ready workflow attached to the comment thread. Worth trying if you want a fully-native pipeline.
- **Model file:** [`wan2.2_animate_14B_bf16.safetensors`](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Wan_2.2_ComfyUI_Repackaged/blob/main/split_files/diffusion_models/wan2.2_animate_14B_bf16.safetensors) (Kijai's link).

### Pose / control

- **Use Sapiens2** for 2D pose estimation. Kijai called it "the current best 2D pose estimator." Feed the **raw Sapiens2 output, not the OpenPose-format conversion** — *djbfilmz* found the raw form works better with Wan Animate.
- **Face is NOT pose-driven.** Kijai: *"WanAnimate doesn't use pose control for face — it's controlled by embeddings and cropped pixels."* So don't waste time tweaking face-pose; tweak the reference image / face crop instead.
- *Kijai* also notes a fully-native WanAnimate workflow should now be possible using SDPose.

### LoRA strengths

- **`lightx2v` strength = 1.2** in Kijai's official workflow (everywhere else it's 1.0). That's intentional — leave it.
- **Speed LoRAs trash detail.** Multiple users (incl. an anonymous wan_chatter post) report `lightx2v` at high strength visibly destroys identity/skin/face quality. If you want max fidelity for a hero shot, **turn lightx2v off and accept the longer render**. (No canonical "without lightx" settings surfaced — several people are actively asking, so this is an open question; default direction is more steps + slightly higher CFG.)
- For style transfer with an existing Wan LoRA → use the **extracted LoRA** form (Kijai).

### Long videos (>5s)

Wan natively maxes at ~5s. Three options people actually use:

1. **Wrapper + auto-loop** (default Kijai behavior, easiest).
2. **Native + context windows** (Ablejones's PR — same idea, native).
3. **WanAnimate's own extension mechanism (causal)** — Ablejones notes this degrades more over time but stays *more temporally consistent*.

**Color shift between windows is the #1 long-video gotcha.** Kijai + Ablejones figured out: apply **a single reference/target frame correction uniformly**, NOT per-frame. Per-frame correction causes the color drift everyone complains about.

### Distance-from-camera (small face) problem

Training data skews close-up, so faces at distance get rescaled badly. *Alisson Pereira's* fix: do a **head swap on the first frame** with Flux Klein 9b and use that as the reference, OR crop the face region → head-swap → restore using Kijai's WanAnimate nodes.

### When NOT to use Wan Animate

- **Animated backgrounds** → use VACE instead (Dream Making's tests at 960×544 / 1280×720). Wan Animate is best for **still BGs**.
- **Full-body motion fidelity** → SCAIL is better. SCAIL is trained on more complex poses; Wan Animate isn't. *But* SCAIL can't do face control or character-replace inpainting — Wan Animate owns that lane.
- **VACE merge attempts** — don't bother. Different architectures, won't combine cleanly (per April 1 wan_chatter summary).

### Iteration tip

*boorayjenkins* — for long gens (he was on a 700-frame shot), **cache the latent to disk** so you can re-run the VAE decoder with different settings without re-sampling for an hour each time. Persists across Comfy restarts. He also caches segmentation masks the same way.

### The community wiki

- **[wanx-troopers.github.io](https://wanx-troopers.github.io/)** (curated by *42hub*) — the up-to-date community knowledge base. Most relevant pages:
  - `/wan-animates.html` — character-replace model comparison
  - `/control.html` — pose / depth / uni3c wiring screenshots
  - `/sigmas.html` — shift / sigma schedule explanations
  - `/loras/part-01.html` — lightx2v versions, steps, strengths

Skill at `~/.claude/skills/banodoco-search/SKILL.md`. Covers:
- the endpoint + anon key + schema

# ArtAgents

A file-based toolkit for agents to make art and creative work alongside a human.

Three kinds of beings live here:

- **Executors** — run one concrete unit of work
- **Orchestrators** — coordinate executors (and other orchestrators) into workflows
- **Elements** — reusable render building blocks (effects, animations, transitions)

`python3 -m artagents` is the executable package gateway. Every summons passes through this one gate.

## First commands

Run from the repository root:

```bash
git status --short
python3 -m artagents --help
python3 -m artagents doctor
python3 -m artagents orchestrators list
python3 -m artagents executors list
python3 -m artagents elements list
python3 -m artagents setup
```

`setup` is dry-run by default; pass `--apply` to mutate.

## Using tools

Find an id:

```bash
python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators|elements] list
```

Inspect to see inputs, outputs, and intent:

```bash
python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators|elements] inspect <id> --json
```

Run it:

```bash
python3 -m artagents [executors|orchestrators] run <id> -- <args>
```

Each tool has its own `STAGE.md` next to its `run.py`. That is the source of truth — read it before invoking. The JSON inspect output points at the folder root and `stage_file`; load only the one relevant `STAGE.md`, not all of them.

At the start of any session that will produce runs, run python3 -m artagents thread show @active first. The [thread] prefix on every command output is your continuous indicator; if it shows the wrong thread, run thread new or pass --thread @new to your next command. Selections are append-only; the most recent write is authoritative on read; prior selections are preserved as history but do not affect current keepers.

Before rendering an iteration video, run `python3 -m artagents.packs.builtin.iteration_video.run inspect <thread>` to see modalities, renderers, quality, cache counts, and estimated cost without rendering.

Use for (a) condensing into a hype cut / sizzle reel / trailer via the full Gemini pipeline, OR (b) lighter "primitive" jobs — transcribe only, split a long video into N smaller videos based on transcript or scene boundaries, extract keyframes, generate an SRT, etc. — by composing individual scripts (transcribe.py, scenes.py, shots.py, cut.py) with a small amount of ad-hoc ffmpeg/Python glue.

# Video Toolkit

The toolkit at `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/banodoco-workspace/tools/` is a set of file-based primitives. Each script reads and writes plain files on disk so you can run any one step alone, inspect its JSON, or wire several together with ffmpeg/Python glue. There is **no required pipeline** — pick what you need.

## Two ways to use this

**Heavy mode — full hype-cut pipeline.** Many Gemini calls, produces one short condensed cut from a long source. Use when the task is "make a hype/sizzle/trailer." Covered in the [Pipeline](#pipeline) section onward.

**Light mode — compose primitives.** No Gemini, no `pipeline.py`, no render. Use when the task is mechanical or only needs one or two stages: "transcribe this," "split on scene boundaries," "chunk on natural pauses," "give me an SRT," "give me 12 × 20-min files." Covered in [Primitive recipes](#primitive-recipes) directly below — read this first if the user did not ask for a hype cut.

## Primitive recipes

Each recipe is a self-contained flow. None of them require the full pipeline; each calls one tool and adds a small amount of ffmpeg or Python.

### Transcript-driven chunking — split a long video at natural speech breaks

Use `transcribe.py` to get word/segment timestamps with silence boundaries, then ffmpeg-cut at the breaks closest to a target chunk length.

```bash
python3 tools/transcribe.py --audio source.mp4 --out work/
# work/transcript.json has segments with start/end timestamps
```

Then a short inline Python script: walk `transcript.json` segments, accumulate duration, and emit a cut whenever the running duration crosses your target AND the current segment ends near a silence (gap between this segment's `end` and next segment's `start` > ~0.5s). Drive `ffmpeg -ss S -to E -c copy out_NN.mp4` from the resulting list.

Stream copy (`-c copy`) is keyframe-aligned. If precise cuts matter, drop `-c copy` and re-encode with `-c:v libx264 -preset fast -crf 20 -c:a aac`.

### Scene-boundary splitting — one output file per detected scene

```bash
python3 tools/scenes.py --video source.mp4 --out work/
# work/scenes.json: [{index, start, end, duration}, ...]
```

Loop over `scenes.json` and ffmpeg-cut. Often you'll filter — drop scenes shorter than ~2s or merge adjacent ones under a minimum length — before emitting files.

### Mechanical chunking — fixed-length splits, no analysis

Skip the toolkit entirely. `ffmpeg -i source.mp4 -c copy -map 0 -segment_time 1200 -f segment -reset_timestamps 1 out_%03d.mp4` produces 20-minute pieces with no transcription or scene detection.

### Transcript-only / SRT-only

`transcribe.py` already emits `transcript.json`, `transcript.srt`, and `transcript.txt`. That's the whole job — no downstream stages needed.

### Keyframe extraction without a hype cut

`shots.py --per-scene N` produces evenly-spaced JPGs per detected scene. Useful for thumbnail grids, contact sheets, or feeding stills to other vision tools.

Everything from here down assumes you're producing a hype cut / sizzle reel / trailer. For any other task, stop and use a [primitive recipe](#primitive-recipes) instead.

---
# ☤ ASCII Video

Renders any content as colored ASCII character video. Audio, video, images, text, or pure math in, MP4/GIF/PNG sequence out. Full RGB color per character cell, 1080p 24fps default. No GPU.

Built for [Hermes Agent](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent). Usable in any coding agent. Canonical source lives here; synced to [`NousResearch/hermes-agent/skills/creative/ascii-video`](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/tree/main/skills/creative/ascii-video) via PR.

## What this is

A skill that teaches an agent how to build single-file Python renderers for ASCII video from scratch. The agent gets the full pipeline: grid system, font rasterization, effect library, shader chain, audio analysis, parallel encoding. It writes the renderer, runs it, gets video.

The output is actual video. Not terminal escape codes. Frames are computed as grids of colored characters, composited onto pixel canvases with pre-rasterized font bitmaps, post-processed through shaders, piped to ffmpeg.

## Modes

| Mode | Input | Output |
|------|-------|--------|
| Video-to-ASCII | A video file | ASCII recreation of the footage |
| Audio-reactive | An audio file | Visuals driven by frequency bands, beats, energy |
| Generative | Nothing | Procedural animation from math |
| Hybrid | Video + audio | ASCII video with audio-reactive overlays |
| Lyrics/text | Audio + timed text (SRT) | Karaoke-style text with effects |
| TTS narration | Text quotes + API key | Narrated video with typewriter text and generated speech |

## Pipeline

Every mode follows the same 6-stage path:

```
INPUT --> ANALYZE --> SCENE_FN --> TONEMAP --> SHADE --> ENCODE
```

1. **Input** loads source material (or nothing for generative).
2. **Analyze** extracts per-frame features. Audio gets 6-band FFT, RMS, spectral centroid, flatness, flux, beat detection with exponential decay. Video gets luminance, edges, motion.
3. **Scene function** returns a pixel canvas directly. Composes multiple character grids at different densities, value/hue fields, pixel blend modes. This is where the visuals happen.
4. **Tonemap** does adaptive percentile-based brightness normalization with per-scene gamma. ASCII on black is inherently dark. Linear multipliers don't work. This does.
5. **Shade** runs a `ShaderChain` (38 composable shaders) plus a `FeedbackBuffer` for temporal recursion with spatial transforms.
6. **Encode** pipes raw RGB frames to ffmpeg for H.264 encoding. Segments concatenated, audio muxed.

## Grid system

Characters render on fixed-size grids. Layer multiple densities for depth.

| Size | Font | Grid at 1080p | Use |
|------|------|---------------|-----|
| xs | 8px | 400x108 | Ultra-dense data fields |
| sm | 10px | 320x83 | Rain, starfields |
| md | 16px | 192x56 | Default balanced |
| lg | 20px | 160x45 | Readable text |
| xl | 24px | 137x37 | Large titles |
| xxl | 40px | 80x22 | Giant minimal |

Rendering the same scene on `sm` and `lg` then screen-blending them creates natural texture interference. Fine detail shows through gaps in coarse characters. Most scenes use two or three grids.

## Character palettes (24)

Each sorted dark-to-bright, each a different visual texture. Validated against the font at init so broken glyphs get dropped silently.

| Family | Examples | Feel |
|--------|----------|------|
| Density ramps | ` .:-=+#@█` | Classic ASCII art gradient |
| Block elements | ` ░▒▓█▄▀▐▌` | Chunky, digital |
| Braille | ` ⠁⠂⠃...⠿` | Fine-grained pointillism |
| Dots | ` ⋅∘∙●◉◎` | Smooth, organic |
| Stars | ` ·✧✦✩✨★✶` | Sparkle, celestial |
| Half-fills | ` ◔◑◕◐◒◓◖◗◙` | Directional fill progression |
| Crosshatch | ` ▣▤▥▦▧▨▩` | Hatched density ramp |
| Math | ` ·∘∙•°±×÷≈≠≡∞∫∑Ω` | Scientific, abstract |
| Box drawing | ` ─│┌┐└┘├┤┬┴┼` | Structural, circuit-like |
| Katakana | ` ·ｦｧｨｩｪｫｬｭ...` | Matrix rain |
| Greek | ` αβγδεζηθ...ω` | Classical, academic |
| Runes | ` ᚠᚢᚦᚱᚷᛁᛇᛒᛖᛚᛞᛟ` | Mystical, ancient |
| Alchemical | ` ☉☽♀♂♃♄♅♆♇` | Esoteric |
| Arrows | ` ←↑→↓↔↕↖↗↘↙` | Directional, kinetic |
| Music | ` ♪♫♬♩♭♮♯○●` | Musical |
| Project-specific | ` .·~=≈∞⚡☿✦★⊕◊◆▲▼●■` | Themed per project |

Custom palettes are built per project to match the content.

## Color strategies

| Strategy | How it maps hue | Good for |
|----------|----------------|----------|
| Angle-mapped | Position angle from center | Rainbow radial effects |
| Distance-mapped | Distance from center | Depth, tunnels |
| Frequency-mapped | Audio spectral centroid | Timbral shifting |
| Value-mapped | Brightness level | Heat maps, fire |
| Time-cycled | Slow rotation over time | Ambient, chill |
| Source-sampled | Original video pixel colors | Video-to-ASCII |
| Palette-indexed | Discrete lookup table | Retro, flat graphic |
| Temperature | Warm-to-cool blend | Emotional tone |
| Complementary | Hue + opposite | Bold, dramatic |
| Triadic | Three equidistant hues | Psychedelic, vibrant |
| Analogous | Neighboring hues | Harmonious, subtle |
| Monochrome | Fixed hue, vary S/V | Noir, focused |

Plus 10 discrete RGB palettes (neon, pastel, cyberpunk, vaporwave, earth, ice, blood, forest, mono-green, mono-amber).

Full OKLAB/OKLCH color system: sRGB↔linear↔OKLAB conversion pipeline, perceptually uniform gradient interpolation, and color harmony generation (complementary, triadic, analogous, split-complementary, tetradic).

## Value field generators (21)

Value fields are the core visual building blocks. Each produces a 2D float array in [0, 1] mapping every grid cell to a brightness value.

### Trigonometric (12)

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| Sine field | Layered multi-sine interference, general-purpose background |
| Smooth noise | Multi-octave sine approximation of Perlin noise |
| Rings | Concentric rings, bass-driven count and wobble |
| Spiral | Logarithmic spiral arms, configurable arm count/tightness |
| Tunnel | Infinite depth perspective (inverse distance) |
| Vortex | Twisting radial pattern, distance modulates angle |
| Interference | N overlapping sine waves creating moire |
| Aurora | Horizontal flowing bands |
| Ripple | Concentric waves from configurable source points |
| Plasma | Sum of sines at multiple orientations/speeds |
| Diamond | Diamond/checkerboard pattern |
| Noise/static | Random per-cell per-frame flicker |
```

```
Install Moirae, a scripted terminal demo video pipeline.

1. Check prerequisites are installed:

   which asciinema agg ffmpeg

   If any are missing:
   - asciinema: brew install asciinema (or pip install asciinema)
   - agg: cargo install --git https://github.com/asciinema/agg
   - ffmpeg: brew install ffmpeg

2. Clone and install Moirae:

   git clone https://github.com/peteromallet/Moirae.git
   cd Moirae
   pip install pillow numpy pyyaml pydantic rich

3. Test it works:

   python -m moirae moirae/scripts/example.yaml

   This should preview a demo in your terminal. To render an MP4:

   python -m moirae moirae/scripts/example.yaml -o demo.mp4

4. Read SKILL.md for the full screenplay YAML schema, scene types,
   camera directives, theme system, and CLI options.

description: Create scripted terminal demo videos of Hermes Agent using the screenplay YAML pipeline. Record, render, and composite polished MP4s with camera zoom/pan, skin theming, and background compositing.
version: 1.0.0
author: Hermes Agent

# Demo Video Pipeline

Create polished terminal demo videos from YAML screenplays. The pipeline records a scripted terminal session, renders it to GIF via agg, then composites to MP4 with camera zoom/pan effects.

## Prerequisites

- `asciinema` — terminal session recording
- `agg` — asciinema GIF renderer ([github.com/asciinema/agg](https://github.com/asciinema/agg))
- `ffmpeg` — video encoding
- Python packages: `pillow`, `numpy`, `pyyaml`, `pydantic`

## Quick Start

```bash
# Preview in terminal (no recording)
python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml

# Record and render to MP4
python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml -o demo.mp4

# With a specific skin
python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml -o demo.mp4 --skin ares

# Dry run (print commands without executing)
python -m demo demo/scripts/example.yaml -o demo.mp4 --dry-run
```

## CLI Options

| Flag | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `script` | Path to YAML screenplay file (required) |
| `-o, --output PATH` | Output MP4 path. If omitted, defaults to `--play` mode |
| `--play` | Preview in terminal without recording |
| `--skin NAME` | Override skin (e.g. `ares`, `mono`, `slate`, `poseidon`) |
| `--typing-speed FLOAT` | Override typing speed (seconds per character) |
| `--dry-run` | Print pipeline commands without executing |
| `--debug-camera` | Print resolved camera keyframe timeline |

## Screenplay YAML Schema

```yaml
title: "My Demo"
skin: "default"              # Skin name (default, ares, mono, slate, poseidon, sisyphus, charizard)
typing_speed: 0.04           # Seconds per character
pause_between: 1.0           # Default pause between scenes

output:
  width: 2560                # Render resolution (2x for sharp text)
  height: 1440
  final_width: 1280          # Output resolution
  final_height: 720
  fps: 30
  font_size: 22
  font_family: "Menlo"
  theme: "github-light"      # agg theme override (omit to use skin default)
  bg_image: "path/to/bg.jpg" # Background image (optional)
  bg_color: "#fdf1de"        # Background fill color (optional)
  bg_opacity: 0.85           # Terminal opacity over background (0.0–1.0)

scenes:
  # ... scene list (see Scene Types below)
```

### Theme and Skin Interaction

The terminal rendering theme comes from the skin's `terminal_theme` field by default. All built-in skins use `github-light`. To override for a specific video, set `output.theme` in the YAML — this takes precedence over the skin.

The compositor's background detection color is derived automatically from the theme via `AGG_THEME_BG` in `skin_engine.py`. Available agg themes: `asciinema`, `dracula`, `github-dark`, `github-light`, `kanagawa`, `kanagawa-dragon`, `kanagawa-light`, `monokai`, `nord`, `solarized-dark`, `solarized-light`, `gruvbox-dark`.

## Scene Types

### Action Scenes

```yaml
# Clear terminal
- action: clear

# Type a shell command with output
- action: type_command
  prefix: "~ $ "
  command: "hermes"
  output: "Starting Hermes Agent..."   # optional

# Show the agent banner
- action: banner
  model: "deephermes-3-llama-3.1-8b"
  context: "128K"
  session_id: "d8f2a1c4"
  tools_count: 24
  skills_count: 42

# Pause
- action: pause
  duration: 1.5

# Print styled text
- action: print
  text: "Hello world"
  color: "#FFD700"

# Standalone camera move
- action: camera
  zoom: 1.0
  duration: 0.8
  ease: "ease-out"
```

### Conversation Scenes

```yaml
- user: "What are the latest developments in AI agents?"
  thinking_time: 3.5
  typing_speed: 0.03          # override per-scene
  pre_pause: 0.5
  post_pause: 0.5
  tools:
    - icon: "🔍"
      verb: "search"
      detail: '"AI agents 2026"'
      duration: "2.1s"
      delay: 0.3
  response: |
    Here are the key developments...
  response_label: " ⚕ Hermes "

  # Camera directives (optional)
  camera:
    zoom: 1.8
    x: 0.5                    # Normalized 0.0–1.0
    y: 0.15
    at: "user_start"          # Timing marker
    duration: 0.8
    ease: "ease-in-out"
  camera_response:
    zoom: 1.4
    y: 0.65
    at: "response_start"
    duration: 0.5
    ease: "ease-in-out"
```

### Camera Directives

Camera directives control zoom and pan during the video. They can be:
- Attached to conversation scenes (`camera:` and `camera_response:`)
- Standalone action scenes (`action: camera`)

| Field | Default | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| `zoom` | 1.0 | Zoom multiplier (1.0 = full frame, 2.0 = 2x zoom) |
| `x` | 0.5 | Horizontal center (0.0 = left, 1.0 = right) |
| `y` | 0.5 | Vertical center (0.0 = top, 1.0 = bottom) |
| `auto_y` | false | Compute y from cursor position at marker time |
| `at` | "scene_start" | Timing marker (`user_start`, `response_start`, `scene_start`) |
| `duration` | 0.5 | Transition time in seconds |
| `ease` | "ease-in-out" | Easing: `linear`, `ease-in`, `ease-out`, `ease-in-out` |

## Pipeline Stages

1. **Record** — `asciinema rec` runs the player in `--play` mode inside a PTY
2. **Render** — `agg` converts the `.cast` recording to a high-res GIF
3. **Composite** — Python reads GIF frames, applies camera crop per-frame, blends background, pipes to `ffmpeg` for MP4 encoding

## Example Screenplays

- `demo/scripts/example.yaml` — Basic conversation demo
- `demo/scripts/example_with_camera.yaml` — Camera zoom/pan effects
- `demo/scripts/hermes_capabilities.yaml` — Full production demo with background image

## Key Files

| File | Role |
|------|------|
| `demo/__main__.py` | CLI entry point |
| `demo/schema.py` | Pydantic models for screenplay YAML |
| `demo/player.py` | Terminal playback engine |
| `demo/pipeline.py` | Orchestrates record → render → composite |
| `demo/recorder.py` | asciinema + agg subprocess wrappers |
| `demo/compositor.py` | GIF frame reader, camera crop, ffmpeg encoding |
| `demo/camera.py` | Keyframe resolution and interpolation |
| `demo/scenes/` | Scene handlers (conversation, action) |
```

## Meta: why I didn't find Moirae

Honest answer — three failures, two of them ArtAgents'.

**My fault.** I had the answer in front of me. When I ran `python3 -m artagents executors list` earlier I saw `external.moirae    external    Moirae` and skipped past it because "Moirae" (the Greek Fates) doesn't pattern-match on "terminal video" in my head. I went grepping for `asciinema|terminal|vhs|termtosvg` instead of just inspecting the unfamiliar names. Lazy.

**ArtAgents' fault — and worth fixing.** Two real gaps:

1. **`executors list` only shows `id | kind | name`.** There's a perfectly good `description` field in every executor manifest (Moirae's says *"Curated metadata for running Moirae against a screenplay to create a video"* — the word "video" alone would have flagged it). It's just not in the list output. A `--long` / `--describe` flag, or making description the default 4th column, would have closed this in seconds.

2. **No capability / keyword search.** `executors search "terminal video"` or `executors search asciinema` doesn't exist. The closest signal Moirae has to "terminal" is `isolation.binaries: [asciinema, agg, ffmpeg]` — buried in the JSON, only visible via `inspect`. So even an agent that knew the right keyword had no path from keyword → executor.

3. **The SKILL.md doesn't tell agents how to discover by capability.** It teaches `executors list` and `executors inspect <id>` but the implicit assumption is *you already know the id*. For a pack ecosystem this only scales if there's a "what can ArtAgents do for X?" entry point.

### Concrete fixes worth considering

- **Cheap:** add `description` to `executors list` default output (or `--describe`).
- **Medium:** add a `keywords:` field to executor manifests and an `executors search <terms>` subcommand that scores against `name + description + keywords + isolation.binaries`. Backfill keywords for the existing ~38 executors (one-shot job; most have an obvious 3-5 word tag set).
- **Free safety net:** in the `artagents` SKILL.md, add a one-liner: *"If you don't know which executor to use, run `executors list --describe | grep -i <topic>` first — don't guess from id alone."* That alone would have caught me today.
- **Bigger:** an `INDEX.md` (or generated `executors/INDEX.md`) — one line per executor grouped by capability domain (video gen, video understanding, audio, terminal, upload, etc). Same shape as the README of a CLI toolbelt.

The current artagents SKILL.md is great at *teaching the protocol* (id → inspect → run) but not at *capability discovery*. Those are different jobs and right now only the first one has tooling.

Want me to take a swing at any of these? The cheapest two (`--describe` flag + a keywords field on Moirae specifically so this query works next time) would take ~5 minutes.

173	def _resolve_marker_time(marker: str, timing) -> Optional[float]:
174	    """Resolve a marker name to an absolute time from scene timing."""
175	    if marker == "scene_start":

183	
184	def _ease(t: float, ease_type: str) -> float:
185	    """Apply easing to normalized t (0.0–1.0)."""
186	    t = max(0.0, min(1.0, t))
187	    if ease_type == "linear":
188	        return t
189	    elif ease_type == "ease-in":
190	        return t * t
191	    elif ease_type == "ease-out":
192	        return 1.0 - (1.0 - t) * (1.0 - t)
193	    elif ease_type == "ease-in-out":
194	        # Smoothstep
195	        return t * t * (3.0 - 2.0 * t)
196	    return t

198	
199	def interpolate_keyframes(
200	    keyframes: List[CameraKeyframe], t: float
201	) -> tuple[float, float, float]:
202	    """Interpolate zoom, x, y at time t given sorted keyframes."""
203	    if not keyframes:
204	        return 1.0, 0.5, 0.5
205	
206	    # Before first keyframe
207	    if t <= keyframes[0].t:
208	        kf = keyframes[0]
209	        return kf.zoom, kf.x, kf.y
210	
211	    # Find the active transition
212	    for i in range(1, len(keyframes)):
213	        kf = keyframes[i]
214	        prev = keyframes[i - 1]
215	        transition_start = kf.t - kf.duration
216	        if t <= kf.t:
217	            if t < transition_start:
218	                return prev.zoom, prev.x, prev.y
219	            # In transition
220	            progress = (t - transition_start) / kf.duration if kf.duration > 0 else 1.0
221	            eased = _ease(progress, kf.ease)
222	            zoom = prev.zoom + (kf.zoom - prev.zoom) * eased
223	            x = prev.x + (kf.x - prev.x) * eased
224	            y = prev.y + (kf.y - prev.y) * eased
225	            return zoom, x, y
226	
227	    # After last keyframe
228	    last = keyframes[-1]
229	    return last.zoom, last.x, last.y

234	def _viewport_bounds(
235	    kf: CameraKeyframe, total_rows: int, total_cols: int,
236	    gif_w: int = 0, gif_h: int = 0,
237	    output_w: int = 1280, output_h: int = 720,
238	):
239	    """Compute visible row/col range, accounting for output aspect ratio.
240	
241	    The compositor crops to the output aspect ratio, which can reduce
242	    the visible height when the GIF is taller than 16:9.
243	    """
244	    output_ar = output_w / output_h if output_h > 0 else 1.78
245	
246	    if gif_w > 0 and gif_h > 0:
247	        # Replicate the compositor's aspect ratio logic
248	        crop_h = gif_h / kf.zoom
249	        crop_w = crop_h * output_ar
250	        if crop_w > gif_w / kf.zoom:
251	            crop_w = gif_w / kf.zoom
252	            crop_h = crop_w / output_ar
253	        char_h = gif_h / total_rows
254	        char_w = gif_w / total_cols
255	        vis_rows = crop_h / char_h
256	        vis_cols = crop_w / char_w
257	    else:
258	        # Fallback without GIF dimensions
259	        vis_rows = total_rows / kf.zoom
260	        vis_cols = total_cols / kf.zoom
261	
262	    center_row = kf.y * total_rows
263	    center_col = kf.x * total_cols
264	    top = max(0, center_row - vis_rows / 2)
265	    bot = min(total_rows, center_row + vis_rows / 2)
266	    left = max(0, center_col - vis_cols / 2)
267	    right = min(total_cols, center_col + vis_cols / 2)
268	    return int(top), int(bot), int(left), int(right)

271	def _load_cast_screens(cast_path, timestamps: List[float], rows: int, cols: int):
272	    """Replay a .cast file through pyte, capturing screen state at each timestamp."""
273	    import json
274	    import pyte
275	
276	    screen = pyte.Screen(cols, rows)
277	    stream = pyte.Stream(screen)
278	
279	    events = []
280	    with open(cast_path) as f:
281	        for i, line in enumerate(f):
282	            if i == 0:
283	                continue
284	            try:
285	                ts, _type, data = json.loads(line)
286	                events.append((ts, data))
287	            except (json.JSONDecodeError, ValueError):
288	                continue
289	
290	    sorted_ts = sorted(set(timestamps))
291	    ts_to_screen: dict[float, list[str]] = {}
292	    event_idx = 0
293	
294	    for target_t in sorted_ts:
295	        while event_idx < len(events) and events[event_idx][0] <= target_t:
296	            stream.feed(events[event_idx][1])
297	            event_idx += 1
298	        ts_to_screen[target_t] = [
299	            screen.buffer[row_idx] for row_idx in range(rows)
300	        ]
301	
302	    result = []
303	    for t in timestamps:
304	        closest = min(sorted_ts, key=lambda st: abs(st - t))
305	        result.append(ts_to_screen[closest])
306	    return result

309	def _render_row(buffer_row: dict, left: int, right: int, max_width: int) -> str:
310	    """Extract visible text from a pyte buffer row within column bounds."""
311	    chars = []
312	    for col in range(left, min(right, left + max_width)):
313	        char = buffer_row.get(col)
314	        if char:
315	            chars.append(char.data if char.data != " " or chars else " ")
316	        else:
317	            chars.append(" ")
318	    return "".join(chars).rstrip()

329	    preview_width: int = 72,
330	) -> str:
331	    """Generate a visual camera timeline with terminal content previews."""
332	    screens = None
333	    if cast_path and cast_path.exists():
334	        try:
335	            screens = _load_cast_screens(
336	                cast_path, [kf.t for kf in keyframes], total_rows, total_cols
337	            )
338	        except Exception:
339	            screens = None
340	
341	    # Load GIF dimensions for accurate aspect-ratio viewport calculation
342	    gif_w, gif_h = 0, 0
343	    if gif_path and gif_path.exists():
344	        try:
345	            from PIL import Image
346	            img = Image.open(gif_path)
347	            gif_w, gif_h = img.size
348	            img.close()
349	        except Exception:
350	            pass
351	
352	    lines = []
353	    ar_info = ""
354	    if gif_w and gif_h:
355	        ar_info = f", GIF {gif_w}×{gif_h}, output {output_w}×{output_h}"
356	    lines.append(
357	        f"Camera Debug  ({len(keyframes)} keyframes, "
358	        f"{total_rows} rows × {total_cols} cols{ar_info})"
359	    )
360	
361	    for i, kf in enumerate(keyframes):
362	        top, bot, left, right = _viewport_bounds(
363	            kf, total_rows, total_cols,
364	            gif_w=gif_w, gif_h=gif_h, output_w=output_w, output_h=output_h,
365	        )
366	        vis_rows = bot - top
367	        vis_cols = right - left
368	
369	        lines.append("")
370	        lines.append("═" * (preview_width + 4))
371	
372	        if i > 0:
373	            prev = keyframes[i - 1]
374	            parts = []
375	            dy = (kf.y - prev.y) * total_rows
376	            if abs(dy) > 0.5:
377	                parts.append(f"pan {'↓' if dy > 0 else '↑'} {abs(dy):.0f} rows")
378	            dx = (kf.x - prev.x) * total_cols
379	            if abs(dx) > 0.5:
380	                parts.append(f"pan {'→' if dx > 0 else '←'} {abs(dx):.0f} cols")
381	            if abs(kf.zoom - prev.zoom) > 0.01:
382	                parts.append(f"zoom {prev.zoom:.1f}x → {kf.zoom:.1f}x")
383	            if parts:
384	                lines.append(f"  ◆ {', '.join(parts)}  ({kf.duration:.1f}s {kf.ease})")
385	            else:
386	                lines.append(f"  ◆ no movement  ({kf.duration:.1f}s)")
387	
388	        lines.append(
389	            f"  t={kf.t:.2f}s  │  {kf.zoom:.1f}x zoom  │  "
390	            f"rows {top}–{bot}  cols {left}–{right}  │  "
391	            f"showing {vis_rows}×{vis_cols} of {total_rows}×{total_cols}"
392	        )
393	
394	        if i < len(keyframes) - 1:
395	            next_kf = keyframes[i + 1]
396	            hold = (next_kf.t - next_kf.duration) - kf.t
397	            if hold > 0.01:
398	                lines.append(f"  holds {hold:.1f}s")
399	            else:
400	                lines.append(f"  immediately transitions →")
401	
402	        if screens:
403	            screen_buf = screens[i]
404	            crop_width = min(vis_cols, preview_width)
405	            lines.append(f"  ┌{'─' * crop_width}┐")
406	            for row_idx in range(top, bot):
407	                if row_idx >= len(screen_buf):
408	                    break
409	                row_text = _render_row(screen_buf[row_idx], left, right, crop_width)
410	                lines.append(f"  │{row_text:<{crop_width}}│")
411	            lines.append(f"  └{'─' * crop_width}┘")
412	
413	    lines.append("")
414	    return "\n".join(lines)
415

> AGENT

Found the follow mode and the resolution cause. Let me fix all three issues:

1. **Resolution:** asciinema is hard-coded to 200×80 cells in `pipeline.py:67-68`. At 1280×720 final, that's ~6 px/cell — unreadable. Fix: bump output to 1920×1080 (or full 2560×1440) and bigger font.
2. **Camera middle-not-left:** there's no auto-x — y is auto-tracked but x is fixed at 0.5. Fix: bias `x: 0.25` to align with the prompt.
3. **Follow mode:** **yes it exists** — `auto_y: true` on the camera directive auto-emits tracking keyframes at `user_end` and at the Q+A midpoint when `response_start` fires, but ONLY if you don't also specify a `camera_response:` block. The current screenplay specifies both, which suppresses follow mode.

Pipeline is\n  asciinema → agg (GIF) → ffmpeg compositor with per-frame camera crop.\n  Repo: https://github.com/peteromallet/Moirae\n---\n\n# Moirae\n\nMoirae turns a YAML **screenplay** into an MP4 of a scripted terminal session.\nYou write the lines, set camera moves, pick a skin — it records, renders, and\ncomposites. No real terminal session is captured; everything is faked\ndeterministically so you can iterate in seconds.\n\nThis skill exists because there are several non-obvious gotchas that produce\nunwatchable output if you don't know about them. **Read the \"Don't ship a bad\nrender\" section before writing your first screenplay.**\n\n## Install (one-time)\n\n```bash\n# Prereqs\nwhich asciinema agg ffmpeg\n# If missing:\n#   asciinema → pip install asciinema  (or brew install asciinema)\n#   agg       → cargo install --git https://github.com/asciinema/agg\n#   ffmpeg    → brew install ffmpeg\npip install pillow numpy pyyaml pydantic rich\n\n# Moirae itself\ngit clone https://github.com/peteromallet/Moirae.git ~/Documents/Moirae\n```\n\nRun from the Moirae checkout:\n\n```bash\ncd ~/Documents/Moirae\npython3 -m moirae path/to/screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4\npython3 -m moirae path/to/screenplay.yaml --play       # terminal preview\npython3 -m moirae path/to/screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --dry-run  # validate only\n```\n\n---\n\n## Don't ship a bad render — pre-flight checklist\n\nThese five mistakes account for ~every \"this looks broken\" first render.\n\n### 1. Final resolution must match the grid\n\nMoirae records the asciinema session at a **fixed 200 cols × 80 rows grid**\n(hardcoded in `pipeline.py`). If your output is smaller than ~9 px per cell\nhorizontally, text is unreadable.\n\n| `final_width` | px per cell | Verdict |\n|---------------|-------------|---------|\n| 1280          | 6.4         | ❌ blurry, illegible |\n| 1920          | 9.6         | ✅ legible |\n| 2560          | 12.8        | ✅ crisp |\n\n**Default to `final_width: 1920, final_height: 1080`.** Render at the same res\n(`width: 1920, height: 1080`) — there's no benefit to rendering then\ndownscaling. Bump `font_size` to 26–32 for a beefier look.\n\n```yaml\noutput:\n  width: 1920\n  height: 1080\n  final_width: 1920\n  final_height: 1080\n  fps: 30\n  font_size: 28\n  font_family: \"Menlo\"\n```\n\n### 2. Use follow mode (`auto_y: true`) — don't hand-aim every camera\n\nMoirae has a real **follow mode** that auto-tracks the cursor through a Q&A\nexchange. Use it. Hand-tuning `y` values for every scene is brittle and the\npan-down happens at the wrong moment because the cursor isn't where you\nguessed.\n\n**The trigger:** `camera.auto_y: true` AND **no** `camera_response:` block.\n\nWhen both conditions hold, Moirae:\n1. Pans to the cursor at `user_start` (where the user prompt begins).\n2. Auto-emits a tracking keyframe at `user_end` (after the prompt is typed).\n3. Auto-emits a keyframe at `response_start` centered on the **Q+A midpoint**\n   so the entire exchange is framed.\n\n```yaml\n- user: \"What's the best workflow?\"\n  response: |\n    Start with Kijai's WanVideoWrapper...\n  camera:\n    zoom: 1.6\n    x: 0.25         # ← see #3\n    auto_y: true    # ← follow mode\n    at: \"user_start\"\n    duration: 0.7\n    ease: \"ease-in-out\"\n  # NOTE: no camera_response — that's what enables follow mode\n```\n\nIf you specify `camera_response:`, follow mode is suppressed and you're back\nto manually picking `y` for every scene. Only do that if you want a custom\nmulti-stage zoom.\n\n### 3. Bias `x` to the left — there's no auto-x\n\n`auto_y` only auto-tracks the **vertical** cursor position. `x` defaults to\n`0.5` (center). Terminal output is left-aligned, so at high zoom the camera\nshows the middle of the terminal — empty whitespace, with the actual prompt\ncropped off at the left edge.\n\n**Fix:** set `x: 0.2` to `0.3` on every conversation camera. At `zoom: 1.6`,\n`x: 0.25` puts the prompt comfortably on-screen with breathing room.\n\n```yaml\ncamera:\n  zoom: 1.6\n  x: 0.25         # ← never leave x at 0.5 for a left-aligned prompt\n  auto_y: true\n```\n\n### 4. Pyenv gotcha — `asciinema: command not found`\n\nIf the user's pyenv global is broken (e.g. set to a Python that isn't\ninstalled), `asciinema` won't resolve even though it's installed under a\ndifferent Python version. Symptom from `python3 -m moirae`:\n\n```\nasciinema recording failed (exit 127): pyenv: asciinema: command not found\nThe `asciinema' command exists in these Python versions: 3.11.11\n```\n\n**Fix:** prepend `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11` (or whichever version has asciinema)\nto the command. Don't try to \"fix\" the user's global pyenv state.\n\n```bash\nPYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4\n```\n\nVerify which Python has asciinema with: `pyenv versions` and\n`ls ~/.pyenv/versions/*/bin/asciinema`.\n\n### 5. Always `--dry-run` first\n\nA full render replays the screenplay in real time (asciinema records live), so\ntypos, missing fields, or an over-long screenplay waste minutes. `--dry-run`\nprints the pipeline commands and exits — catches schema errors and shows the\nfinal pipeline parameters in <1s.\n\n```bash\npython3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --dry-run\n```\n\n---\n\n## Screenplay anatomy\n\n```yaml\ntitle: \"My Demo\"\nskin: \"ares\"               # default | ares | mono | slate | poseidon | sisyphus | charizard\ntyping_speed: 0.035        # seconds per character (lower = faster)\npause_between: 0.9         # default seconds between scenes\n\noutput:\n  width: 1920\n  height: 1080\n  final_width: 1920\n  final_height: 1080\n  fps: 30\n  font_size: 28\n  font_family: \"Menlo\"\n  bg_color: \"#0b0b10\"      # optional terminal bg fill\n  bg_opacity: 0.92         # 0–1, terminal opacity over background\n  bg_image: \"path/to/bg.jpg\"  # optional background image\n  theme: \"github-light\"    # agg theme override (see Skins)\n\nscenes:\n  - action: clear\n  - action: banner\n    model: \"claude-opus-4-7\"\n    context: \"1M\"\n    session_id: \"demo\"\n    tools_count: 12\n    skills_count: 24\n  - action: type_command\n    prefix: \"~ $ \"\n    command: \"do-the-thing arg\"\n    output: \"result line\"        # optional\n  - action: pause\n    duration: 0.6\n  - action: print\n    text: \"↳ note\"\n    color: \"#9ad7ff\"\n  - action: camera                # standalone camera move\n    zoom: 1.0\n    duration: 0.9\n    ease: \"ease-out\"\n\n  - user: \"User prompt text here\"\n    thinking_time: 2.4            # seconds of \"thinking\" before tools/response\n    pre_pause: 0.3\n    post_pause: 0.5\n    typing_speed: 0.03            # per-scene override\n    tools:\n      - icon: \"🔍\"\n        verb: \"search\"\n        detail: '\"some query\"'\n        duration: \"1.4s\"\n        delay: 0.2\n    response: |\n      Multi-line response.\n      **Markdown bold** renders via rich.\n    response_label: \" ⚕ Hermes \"\n    camera:\n      zoom: 1.6\n      x: 0.25\n      auto_y: true\n      at: \"user_start\"            # user_start | user_end | response_start | scene_start | scene_end\n      duration: 0.7\n      ease: \"ease-in-out\"         # linear | ease-in | ease-out | ease-in-out\n    # Omit camera_response to enable follow mode (see #2 above)\n```\n\n---\n\n## Camera mental model\n\nThe **viewport** is the visible portion of the 200×80 grid:\n\n- `zoom: 1.0` → see all 200×80 cells (full frame)\n- `zoom: 2.0` → see 100×40 cells centered on `(x, y)`\n- `(x, y)` are normalized 0–1; `(0, 0)` is top-left, `(1, 1)` is bottom-right\n\nAt `zoom: 1.6, x: 0.25`, you see ~125 cols starting roughly at col 25 — perfect\nfor a left-aligned prompt area. At `x: 0.5` (default), you'd see cols 37–162,\nmissing the leftmost 37 cols where the prompt actually is.\n\nUse `--debug-camera` to print the resolved keyframe timeline with content\npreviews — invaluable when a zoom looks wrong.\n\n```bash\npython3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --debug-camera\n```\n\n---\n\n## Skins\n\nBuilt-in skins (set `skin:` in the screenplay):\n\n- `default` — neutral light\n- `ares` — dark, terminal-y\n- `mono` — black & white\n- `slate` — muted gray\n- `poseidon` — blue-tinted\n- `sisyphus` — earthy\n- `charizard` — warm orange/red\n\nSkins set the agg theme, banner colors, and tool-icon palette. Override the\ntheme alone via `output.theme` (e.g. `github-light`, `dracula`, `monokai`,\n`nord`, `solarized-dark`, `gruvbox-dark`).\n\n---\n\n## When to use Moirae\n\n✅ **Good fit:**\n- Agent demo videos (\"ask Claude X, watch it answer\")\n- Tutorial reels showing a CLI workflow\n- Polished terminal screencasts where typing rhythm matters\n- Animated Q&A explainers in a coding-agent aesthetic\n\n❌ **Wrong tool:**\n- Real terminal recordings (just use `asciinema rec` directly)\n- Long-form (>2 min) — playback is real-time, screenplay gets unwieldy\n- Anything needing a real shell with side effects (Moirae fakes everything)\n\n---\n\n## Cheatsheet — the recipe that just works\n\n```yaml\ntitle: \"...\"\nskin: \"ares\"\ntyping_speed: 0.035\npause_between: 0.9\n\noutput:\n  width: 1920\n  height: 1080\n  final_width: 1920\n  final_height: 1080\n  fps: 30\n  font_size: 28\n  font_family: \"Menlo\"\n\nscenes:\n  - action: clear\n  - action: banner          # optional\n    model: \"...\"\n    session_id: \"...\"\n\n  - user: \"Question 1?\"\n    thinking_time: 2.0\n    response: |\n      Answer 1...\n    camera:\n      zoom: 1.6\n      x: 0.25\n      auto_y: true\n      at: \"user_start\"\n      duration: 0.7\n\n  - user: \"Question 2?\"\n    thinking_time: 1.5\n    response: |\n      Answer 2...\n    camera: {zoom: 1.55, x: 0.25, auto_y: true, at: \"user_start\", duration: 0.6}\n\n  - action: camera          # zoom out at the end\n    zoom: 1.0\n    duration: 0.9\n    ease: \"ease-out\"\n```\n\nRender:\n\n```bash\nPYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4 --dry-run  # check\nPYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 python3 -m moirae screenplay.yaml -o out.mp4            # render\nopen out.mp4\n```\n"
}

# Plan: ArtAgents skill / docs / install architecture

## 1. Naming + locations

Three concerns, three homes — keep them physically separate so nothing fights the in-flight discovery work.

| Concern | Location | Audience |
|---|---|---|
| Pack-author guide | `docs/authoring-packs.md` (long-form) + a one-page `docs/PACK_CHECKLIST.md` | A human writing a new pack |
| Per-folder template (built-in) | `docs/templates/executor/` (already exists — flesh it out) and `docs/templates/orchestrator/` | A human copying a sibling |
| Per-folder template (external) | New `docs/templates/external_executor/` | Authors wrapping an upstream tool |
| Per-pack installable skill | `artagents/packs/<pack>/<slug>/skill/SKILL.md` (optional folder) | The end user installing into `~/.claude/skills` |
| Top-level skill | unchanged: `/SKILL.md` (symlinked into `~/.claude/skills/artagents/`) | Agents using ArtAgents |
| Install CLI | `artagents/skills_cli.py`, wired into `artagents/pipeline.py` next to `setup_cli` | End user |
| Optional pack-level skill manifest | `artagents/packs/<pack>/<slug>/skill.yaml` | Install command (declares source + target) |

Rationale for `skill/` as a sub-folder rather than a top-level `SKILL.md` per pack: keeps the discovery surface (manifest + `STAGE.md`) clean, lets the install copy/symlink one directory verbatim into `~/.claude/skills/<name>/`, and supports skills that ship multiple files (assets, references, `scripts/`).

## 2. Pack-author guide outline (`docs/authoring-packs.md`)

Headings only; concrete on what each section must mention.

- **What is a pack** — built-in vs external vs domain (iteration, upload). One-paragraph each.
- **The three artifact types** — executor, orchestrator, element. Cross-link to existing `docs/creating-tools.md` (do not duplicate decision rule — link).
- **Required files (must-have)**
  - `pack.yaml` (id, name, version) at pack root
  - Per-tool: `executor.yaml` or `orchestrator.yaml` with `id`, `name`, `kind`, `short_description`, `keywords`, `inputs`, `outputs`, `command`, `cache`, `isolation` — call out that `short_description` and `keywords` are **required for discovery** (the in-flight `search` subcommand reads them)
  - Per-tool: `run.py` exposing `main(argv)`
  - Per-tool: `STAGE.md` (see §4 for the rule)
- **Optional files (nice-to-have)**
  - `skill/SKILL.md` + `skill.yaml` if this pack should ship an installable Claude Code skill
  - `requirements.txt` (external packs only)
  - `src/` private helpers
  - tests under `tests/`
- **External pack specifics** — `kind: external`, `isolation.binaries`, `isolation.requirements`, `metadata.homepage`, `metadata.manifest_only: true`. Pointer to upstream README rather than duplicating docs.
- **Naming + id rules** — `<pack>.<slug>` qualified; element ids stay bare; first segment of id must equal pack id. (Already enforced — restate for completeness.)
- **The `STAGE.md` vs `SKILL.md` rule** — embed §4.
- **Discovery contract** — what `list`, `search`, `inspect` will surface from your manifest. Why `short_description` matters (it lands in the SKILL.md capability index).
- **After you add a pack** — run `python3 scripts/gen_capability_index.py`, run `python3 -m artagents doctor`, write a focused test under `tests/`.
- **Worked example** — link to the canonical template folder from §3.

## 3. The folder templates

**Canonical built-in template — flesh out `docs/templates/executor/`:**

| File | Currently | Should demonstrate |
|---|---|---|

## 4. STAGE.md vs SKILL.md — the rule

> **`STAGE.md`** is for an agent **already inside ArtAgents** that just ran `inspect <id>`. It answers: "what is this tool, what's the canonical command, what artifact goes in, what comes out." Keep it short, command-forward, and assume the reader has the rest of the repo. Built-in: write it in full. External: keep it thin and point upstream.
>
> **`SKILL.md`** is for an agent in a **different harness** that has installed this skill into `~/.claude/skills/`. It answers: "when should I reach for this tool at all, what gotchas blow up the first render, full schema, install steps." Standalone document; assumes nothing about the surrounding repo. Top-level `/SKILL.md` plays this role for ArtAgents itself; pack-level `skill/SKILL.md` plays it for individual installable tools (Moirae is the model — see `~/.claude/skills/moirae/SKILL.md`).

Rule of thumb: if you'd say it inside an ArtAgents session, it's STAGE; if it's onboarding someone who just installed the skill cold, it's SKILL.

## 5. Install command surface

New module `artagents/skills_cli.py`, registered in `pipeline.py` alongside `setup`. CLI:

```
python3 -m artagents skills list                       # all installable skills (top-level + per-pack)
python3 -m artagents skills inspect <name>             # show source, target, current install state
python3 -m artagents skills install <name> [--target ~/.claude/skills] [--mode symlink|copy] [--force]
python3 -m artagents skills install --all
python3 -m artagents skills uninstall <name>
```

Discovery: walk `artagents/packs/*/*/skill.yaml` plus the implicit top-level `/SKILL.md`. Each `skill.yaml` declares:

```yaml
name: moirae                        # target dir under ~/.claude/skills/
source: local | upstream
path: ./skill/SKILL.md              # if local
upstream:                           # if upstream
  repo: https://github.com/peteromallet/Moirae
  ref: main                         # or a tag/sha
  path: SKILL.md
```

**Recommendation — local copy is canonical, with a sync command for upstream:**

- Default: pack ships the SKILL.md **in-repo** under `skill/SKILL.md`. Source-of-truth is the pack folder. This wins on offline use, version pinning, no network at install time, and reviewable diffs in PRs.
- For packs whose canonical doc lives upstream (Moirae, vibecomfy), add a separate `python3 -m artagents skills sync <name>` that fetches the upstream file and writes it to `skill/SKILL.md`. Run via `gh api` or `curl` of the raw file at the pinned `ref`. Commit the result. Keeps install hermetic; freshness is an explicit author action, not an end-user surprise.
- Reject "clone the upstream repo at install time" — too slow, breaks offline, no version pinning, and three-second installs become thirty.

**File-copy semantics — symlink for local, copy for upstream-synced:**

- Default `--mode symlink` for `source: local`, mirroring the existing top-level `~/.claude/skills/artagents` symlink. Live edits to the pack appear immediately in the harness — matches today's developer ergonomics.
- `--mode copy` is the only option for upstream-synced files (you don't want a symlink into a transient checkout). Skill content is part of the repo; copy means "snapshot at install time."
- `--mode copy` available as an opt-in on local skills for users who want a frozen snapshot.

**Idempotency / overwrite:**

- If `~/.claude/skills/<name>` doesn't exist → create.
- If it exists and is a symlink to the same target → no-op, exit 0.
- If it exists and points elsewhere or is a real dir → refuse unless `--force`. Print a one-line diagnosis (where it points, when it was last modified) so the user can decide.
- `install --all` continues past per-skill conflicts and prints a summary table.

## 6. Migration plan

| Pack | Today | Change |
|---|---|---|
| Top-level `/SKILL.md` | exists, symlinked | unchanged |
| `builtin/*` STAGE.md | many are 2-line stubs (transcribe, quote_scout, foley_map, iteration_video, vary_grid, logo_ideas) | re-author against new template — small, mostly mechanical |
| `external/moirae` | thin STAGE.md, no skill folder | add `skill/SKILL.md` (sync from `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/SKILL.md`) + `skill.yaml` with `source: upstream` |
| `external/vibecomfy` | thin STAGE.md, no skill folder | add `skill/SKILL.md` (sync from upstream) + `skill.yaml` |
| `external/fal_foley` | reasonable STAGE.md, no installable skill | add `skill/SKILL.md` if it deserves one; otherwise skip — not every pack needs an installable skill |
| `iteration/*`, `upload/*` | STAGE.md exists | unchanged unless the new authoring guide flags drift |

Backwards compatibility: none of this breaks the current `inspect`/`run` paths — `skill/` and `skill.yaml` are additive, ignored by today's loaders. `STAGE.md` content changes are doc-only.

## 7. Risks / open calls

- **Naming collision.** `python3 -m artagents skills` reads naturally but gets close to `~/.claude/skills/`. Consider `... skill install` (singular) or `... claude-skills install`. Decide before shipping.
- **Top-level SKILL.md as a pack skill.** Today the top-level `/SKILL.md` is symlinked manually into `~/.claude/skills/artagents/`. Should `skills install --all` adopt that symlink (idempotent re-creation) or leave it alone? Recommendation: adopt it — the install command should own every link in `~/.claude/skills/`.
- **Upstream sync auth.** Moirae and vibecomfy are public; fine. Anything private would need `gh api` with a token — defer until a private pack actually needs it.
- **`docs/templates/` vs `artagents/packs/builtin/<reference>/`.** Two-tier templates (skeleton in `docs/templates/`, fleshed-out reference under `builtin/`) duplicates content. Recommendation: keep `docs/templates/` as the *copy-this* skeleton and call out one `builtin/transcribe/` as the *read-this-too* reference; don't try to make one folder both.
- **Discovery agent's `search` interaction.** Make sure `short_description` and `keywords` requirements I'm enshrining in the authoring guide match exactly what the in-flight schema work lands on. Hold the guide PR until that lands; the rest (templates, install CLI) is independent.
- **Validation in `doctor`.** Worth adding a `doctor` check that every pack with a `skill/` folder has a `skill.yaml`, and every `skill.yaml` resolves to a readable `SKILL.md`? Cheap, catches drift.

# ArtAgents Multi-Harness Skill Install — Plan

## Research findings (so we're working from facts)

**AGENTS.md is real.** Stewarded by the Linux Foundation's Agentic AI Foundation; backed by OpenAI Codex, Jules, Cursor, Aider, Continue, Factory, Amp, Zed, Warp, opencode, goose, and Copilot (CLI + IDE). It's plain markdown with no required frontmatter — agents just parse the text. Project-level adoption is broad; system-level adoption is uneven.

**Per-harness user-level surfaces (verified):**

| Harness | User-level path | Format | Trigger |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description` required) + markdown | Keyword/description match (model-invoked) |
| Codex CLI | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (also `AGENTS.override.md`, `TEAM_GUIDE.md`, `.agents.md`); also `~/.codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (Agent Skills, parallel to Claude) | Plain markdown (AGENTS.md); SKILL.md w/ frontmatter for Skills | AGENTS.md always-loaded; Skills model-invoked |
| Cursor | **No real user-level rules file on disk** — User Rules live in Cursor Settings UI (synced via account). Project rules at `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` only. ([forum confirmation](https://forum.cursor.com/t/user-based-cursor-rules/119894)) | `.mdc` (markdown + optional frontmatter `description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply`) | Glob/description match |
| Aider | `~/.aider.conf.yml` with `read: [path...]`; the read targets are markdown (commonly `CONVENTIONS.md`) | Plain markdown loaded via config | Always-loaded once configured |
| Copilot CLI | `$HOME/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` | Plain markdown | Always-loaded |
| Copilot VS Code | No real user-level (workspace-level only via `.github/copilot-instructions.md`); JetBrains supports `~/.config/github-copilot/global-copilot-instructions.md` | Plain markdown | Always-loaded |
| Continue.dev | `~/.continue/config.yaml` `rules:` array, **or** drop `.md` files into `~/.continue/rules/` | Markdown strings / files | Always-loaded |

**Frontmatter compatibility.** A YAML frontmatter block at the top of a markdown file is benign for every harness *except* Claude/Cursor where it carries semantics. Claude requires `name` + `description`; Cursor uses different keys (`description`, `globs`, `alwaysApply`). So a single physical file CAN satisfy Claude + AGENTS.md consumers (Codex, Aider, Copilot CLI, Continue), but Cursor needs a separate frontmatter shape, and Aider/Copilot/Continue treat the YAML as visible markdown unless we hide it (it renders as a `---` table, harmless but ugly). One file with Claude-style frontmatter is the pragmatic 80% solution; Cursor is an adapter.

**Symlink tolerance.** All these tools open files via normal stdlib reads — symlinks are transparent. No watcher quirks observed. macOS/Linux fine; Windows needs admin or Developer Mode for symlinks (use junctions or copies as fallback).

**Current ArtAgents state.** The repo has one top-level `SKILL.md` (with Claude frontmatter) and an `AGENTS.md` symlink to it. `~/.claude/skills/artagents → ArtAgents` (whole-repo symlink). `~/.codex/skills/artagents` is the same pattern. There are NO per-pack `SKILL.md` files inside `artagents/packs/*` yet — Moirae and banodoco-search are *separate* repos that ship their own. So "auto-discover per-pack skills" today means *zero* pack docs to discover; this plan is largely greenfield for in-repo packs.

---

## A. Source-of-truth shape — recommend (ii) one `SKILL.md` per pack + generator

Each ArtAgents pack owns `artagents/packs/<pack>/SKILL.md` with Claude frontmatter (`name: artagents-<pack>`, `description: …`). A generator emits per-harness adapter files at install time. The top-level `SKILL.md` stays as the umbrella entry.

**Why not just AGENTS.md per pack:** Claude Code and Codex Skills both *require* the `SKILL.md` filename + frontmatter; AGENTS.md doesn't satisfy them. Going SKILL-first means our canonical files work for the two harnesses with the strictest semantics, and downgrading to plain markdown for Aider/Copilot/Continue is trivial (strip frontmatter, optionally rename).

**What we lose:** can't just point a brand-new harness at the raw repo and say "you'll find AGENTS.md everywhere" — they'll see SKILL.md instead. Mitigation: keep the top-level `AGENTS.md → SKILL.md` symlink and have `skills install` drop AGENTS.md aliases per pack on disk (cheap).

## B. Per-harness install map

| Harness | Target path on disk | What we drop | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/artagents-<pack>/SKILL.md` (+ subdirs) | Symlink to `<repo>/artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/` directory | **Symlink dir** |
| Codex Skills | `~/.codex/skills/artagents-<pack>/SKILL.md` | Same skill dir | **Symlink dir** |
| Codex AGENTS.md | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` | Stanza appended (between `<!-- artagents:begin -->` / `:end -->` markers) listing all packs and pointing at full SKILL.md paths | **Generated, idempotent block** |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/rules/artagents-<pack>.mdc` (note: this is a real user-config dir on macOS — the docs say it's UI-only, but the dir exists & loads) | Generated `.mdc` with Cursor frontmatter (`description`, `alwaysApply: false`) wrapping pack content | **Generated copy** (frontmatter differs) |
| Aider | `~/.aider.conf.yml` `read:` list pointing at `<repo>/artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/CONVENTIONS.md` | Edit `read:` list (preserve other entries); CONVENTIONS.md is a symlink to SKILL.md (Aider tolerates frontmatter) | **YAML edit + symlink** |
| Copilot CLI | `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` | Generated stanza w/ markers | **Generated block** |
| Copilot JetBrains | `~/.config/github-copilot/global-copilot-instructions.md` | Same generated block | **Generated block** |
| Continue.dev | `~/.continue/rules/artagents-<pack>.md` | Symlink to pack skill (frontmatter rendered but harmless) | **Symlink file** |

**Convention:** every pack ships `artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/SKILL.md` (and optional `scripts/`, `references/`). The top-level repo `SKILL.md` becomes `artagents-core` and lives at `<repo>/skill/SKILL.md` (with a top-level symlink for backward compat).

## C. Install CLI surface

```
python3 -m artagents skills list
```
Prints a table: pack name, short_description (reuses the `short_description` field already added in capability-discovery work), per-harness target paths, current-installed status (✓/✗/stale).

```
python3 -m artagents skills install <pack> [--harness …|all]
```
Detects available harnesses by probing: `~/.claude/`, `~/.codex/`, `~/.cursor/`, `~/.aider.conf.yml` (or create on first install if `--harness aider` explicit), `~/.copilot/`, `~/.config/github-copilot/`, `~/.continue/`. Default `--harness all` = all *detected* (never creates a harness home). Each adapter is a small class: `plan() → list[Action]`, `apply()`, `verify()`. Idempotent.

```
python3 -m artagents skills install --all
```
Walks `artagents/packs/*/skill/SKILL.md` + top-level `skill/SKILL.md`, runs `install` for each detected harness.

```
python3 -m artagents skills sync
```
Same as `install --all`, but also **prunes** orphaned symlinks/blocks (packs that no longer exist) and **refreshes** generated content (Cursor `.mdc`, AGENTS.md blocks). This is the command users run after `git pull`.

```
python3 -m artagents skills uninstall <pack> [--harness …]
```
Removes symlinks, deletes generated files, surgically removes marker blocks from AGENTS.md / copilot-instructions / aider.conf.yml.

```
python3 -m artagents skills doctor
```
(Bonus, low cost.) Verifies every install target points at the right file, frontmatter parses, no orphans. Hooks into existing `python3 -m artagents doctor`.

## D. Auto-update story for new packs — recommend hybrid (i) + (ii)

**One repo-wide symlink per harness that supports tree-walk discovery, per-pack symlinks where it doesn't.**

- **Claude Code** wants flat `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` — does NOT walk trees. Per-pack symlinks required. Today's `~/.claude/skills/artagents → ArtAgents` only works because the repo *itself* has a top-level SKILL.md; it doesn't expose pack skills. New pack ⇒ new symlink ⇒ `skills sync` is mandatory.
- **Codex Skills**: same constraint as Claude — flat. Per-pack symlinks.
- **Codex AGENTS.md**: a single managed block; regenerated by `sync` to list current packs.
- **Cursor**: flat `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc`. Per-pack generated files.
- **Aider**: `read:` list — append per pack on `sync`.
- **Continue / Copilot**: flat dir or single block — same pattern.

**No daemon.** A filesystem watcher is overkill — the natural sync points are `git pull` and `git checkout`. Wire `skills sync` into a post-merge / post-checkout git hook (opt-in, off by default). Research landed. Top-line answers:

**AGENTS.md is a real cross-tool standard** — adopted by Codex, Cursor, Aider, Continue, Copilot, Jules, Zed, Warp, Factory. **But** it's a *project-level* convention. At system/user level there is **no single path all harnesses check** — each one has its own home:

| Harness | User-level path | Format |
|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` | YAML frontmatter required |
| Codex CLI | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` *and* `~/.codex/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` (both!) | Plain MD / SKILL.md |
| Cursor | `~/.cursor/rules/*.mdc` (works on disk, *officially UI-only*) | Different frontmatter schema |
| Aider | `~/.aider.conf.yml` `read:` list | Markdown via config |
| Copilot CLI | `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` | Plain MD |
| Copilot JetBrains | `~/.config/github-copilot/global-copilot-instructions.md` | Plain MD |
| Continue | `~/.continue/rules/*.md` | Markdown |

So one canonical doc per pack is achievable, but it needs an **adapter layer** that fans out to each harness's quirks (Cursor needs different frontmatter, AGENTS.md is a managed block, Aider edits YAML, Claude/Codex want flat dirs).

- **Source of truth:** `artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/SKILL.md` per pack (Claude frontmatter), promote top-level to `_core` pack for symmetry. Single source, multiple targets.

# Revised plan: Claude Code + Codex + Hermes

## A. Compatibility verdict

**Yes — one physical `artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/SKILL.md` plus its `references/` subdir satisfies all three harnesses via symlinks alone, no per-harness adapters.** All three load the same shape: a directory containing `SKILL.md` with `name` + `description` YAML frontmatter, and Hermes follows symlinks during discovery (`os.walk(..., followlinks=True)`, `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/hermes-agent/agent/skill_utils.py:446`). Hermes-specific extras live under `metadata.hermes.*` — Claude/Codex ignore unknown frontmatter keys, so the same file is portable.

Caveats, neither requires an adapter: Hermes preprocesses `${HERMES_SKILL_DIR}`, `${HERMES_SESSION_ID}`, and inline `` !`shell` `` in skill content (`/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/hermes-agent/agent/skill_preprocessing.py:12-20`). If a pack avoids those tokens, content is identical across harnesses.

## B. Per-harness install map

| Harness | Path | Mechanism | Caveats |
|---|---|---|---|
| Claude Code | `~/.claude/skills/<pack>/` | symlink dir → `artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/` | confirmed slot already in use (`~/.claude/skills/artagents` exists) |
| Codex | `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (append block) + `~/.codex/skills/<pack>/` symlink dir | generated managed block in `AGENTS.md` referencing the symlinked dir | Codex has no native skill loader; the AGENTS.md block tells the model "if user asks X, read `~/.codex/skills/<pack>/SKILL.md`". Block is fenced with `<!-- artagents:begin --> … <!-- artagents:end -->` for idempotent rewrite. |
| Hermes | `~/.hermes/skills/<pack>/` | symlink dir → `artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/` | Override via `HERMES_HOME` env var (`hermes_constants.py:14`). Alternative without symlinks: add the artagents packs root to `skills.external_dirs` in `~/.hermes/config.yaml` (`agent/skill_utils.py:174-232`) — one config line covers all packs. |

## C. CLI surface

```
artagents install <pack> [--harness claude|codex|hermes|all] [--dry-run] [--force]
artagents uninstall <pack> [--harness …]
artagents list-installed
artagents doctor
```

Auto-detection (`--harness all` default) probes only:
- `~/.claude/` → claude
- `~/.codex/` → codex
- `~/.hermes/` or `$HERMES_HOME` → hermes

`doctor` resolves each symlink, parses each `SKILL.md` frontmatter, and reports drift.

## D. Hermes specifics worth highlighting

1. **`metadata.hermes.config`** — Hermes lets a skill declare config.yaml vars it needs (`skill_utils.py:269-325`). If an artagents pack has runtime config (API keys, paths), declaring them here triggers Hermes' first-run prompt; Claude/Codex ignore the block. Cheap win.
2. **Conditional activation** — `metadata.hermes.requires_toolsets` / `fallback_for_tools` (`skill_utils.py:258-263`) gate skills on tool availability. Useful for packs that require ffmpeg, comfyui, etc.
3. **Hermes follows symlinks**; Hermes accepts `external_dirs` — so a single config edit can register the entire `artagents/packs/` tree without per-pack symlinks. Worth offering as `--mechanism external-dir` for hermes.
4. **Avoid `${HERMES_*}` tokens and `` !`shell` `` in pack content** unless gated — they survive on Claude/Codex as literal text. Document as a content rule for pack authors.

## E. Open calls

1. **Frontmatter shape:** single shape works. Standard `name` + `description` for all three; optional `metadata.hermes.{config,requires_toolsets,fallback_for_*}` block when relevant. No generator needed.
2. **Hermes mechanism default:** symlink-per-pack (parity with claude/codex) or `external_dirs` config edit (one-shot, all packs)? Recommend symlink default for parity, expose `--mechanism external-dir` as opt-in.
3. **Codex managed block format:** confirm the marker pair (`<!-- artagents:begin -->` / `<!-- artagents:end -->`) and whether it lives in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` (global) or per-project `AGENTS.md`. User-level scope is the stated target, so global.
4. **Pack content rule:** forbid `${HERMES_*}` / `` !`…` `` in shared `SKILL.md`, or allow them and accept Claude/Codex see literals?

Schema:\n  ```json\n  {\n    \"version\": 1,\n    \"installs\": {\n      \"claude\": {\"_core\": {\"target\": \"...\", \"installed_at\": \"...\", \"mechanism\": \"symlink\"}, ...},\n      \"codex\":  {...},\n      \"hermes\": {...}\n    },\n    \"nudge\": {\n      \"claude\": {\"last_shown_at\": \"...\"},\n      \"codex\":  {\"last_shown_at\": \"...\"},\n      \"hermes\": {\"last_shown_at\": \"...\"}\n    }\n  }\n  ```\n- `harnesses/__init__.py`, `harnesses/base.py` — abstract `HarnessAdapter` with `detect()`, `target_for(pack_id) -> Path`, `plan(action, pack)`, `apply(action, pack)`, `verify(pack)`, `uninstall(pack)`.\n- `harnesses/claude.py` — symlinks `~/.claude/skills/artagents-<pack>` → `<repo>/artagents/packs/<pack>/skill/`. `detect()` returns True if `~/.claude/` exists. Special case: `_core` installs as `~/.claude/skills/artagents/` (preserving the existing path).\n- `harnesses/codex.py` — symlinks `~/.codex/skills/artagents-<pack>/` AND maintains a fenced block in `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` listing each pack with its `short_description` and target path. - `description`: *"ArtAgents pipeline step: editor_review."* ← lazy stub, worse than the short

- (b) Drop the empty/stub `description` fields and let `inspect` fall back to `short_description` (5 min mechanical edit)

> AGENT

**Found the bug** — and it's not just slow, it's an actual deadlock. Moirae passes `stderr=subprocess.PIPE` to ffmpeg but **never reads stderr during encode**. ffmpeg with `-preset slow` writes per-frame progress to stderr; when the OS pipe buffer fills (~64 KB), ffmpeg blocks on stderr write, Moirae blocks waiting to push more frames into stdin → permanent deadlock. Overnight sleep likely tipped a borderline case over.

Killing the stuck processes, patching Moirae locally to (a) drain stderr to a file, (b) use `fast` preset (still good quality, much less CPU). Then re-rendering.

> AGENT

The composite is running as background task `bi6lf19v3`. With the new fast preset + stderr drain bug fixed, this should finish in a minute or so (vs 15+ hours stuck). I'll get a notification when it completes; opening the file at that point.

Summary of what was wrong and what I changed:

**Root cause:** Moirae's `compositor.py` passes `stderr=subprocess.PIPE` to ffmpeg but never reads from that pipe. With `-preset slow`, ffmpeg writes per-frame stats to stderr, the OS pipe buffer fills (~64 KB), ffmpeg blocks on its next stderr write, and Moirae blocks trying to push more frames into stdin. Permanent deadlock. Last night's sleep tipped it over.

**Two-line fix in `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/moirae/compositor.py`:**
- Redirect stderr to a `<output>.ffmpeg.log` file instead of an unread pipe.
- Switch preset from `slow` → `fast` (still good quality, ~10× faster encode).

**Worth PRing upstream** — the deadlock is a real bug. The proper fix is either (a) drain stderr in a thread or (b) just pipe stderr to a file/DEVNULL. I went with (b) since it's simpler.

Skipping steps 1 and 2 entirely this time by reusing the existing `.cast`, `.gif`, and `_timing.json` from the killed run — going straight to composite. Will fire the open command once `bi6lf19v3` completes.

> AGENT

Found it — three real issues, all fixable.

**The "weird white with grey outlines" / "weird Hermes banner":** all skins default to `github-light` (dark text on white bg). The screenplay has `bg_color: "#0b0b10"` at `bg_opacity: 0.92`, so the compositor blends a light-themed terminal over a dark background. That's why dark text on white reads as ghostly grey-on-dark with halos. **Need a dark theme + drop the conflicting bg_color override.**

**The "bottom of screen after Q4":** terminal is 80 rows hardcoded. By Q4 you've scrolled past row 60. Auto-follow stays glued near the bottom because that's where the cursor is. Two ways to fix: drop one of the Q&As, or `action: clear` mid-conversation. The closing full zoom-out is just the explicit `action: camera zoom:1.0` — drop that and it ends gracefully.

**"Typing looks good vs sent looks weird":** same root cause as the theme issue — the cursor is rendered with the bright cursor color which is legible, but committed text uses the theme foreground color which then gets blended weird.

Patching the screenplay (dark theme, drop bg overrides, drop closing zoom-out, single clear before Q4 to reset):
