{
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/moirae/fonts/__init__.py",
  "content": "\"\"\"Bundled fonts + a one-time install-or-warn helper.\n\nMoirae ships a Nerd Font (JetBrains Mono Nerd Font Mono — OFL) so renders\nthat hit non-ASCII glyphs (Braille caduceus, dingbats, box drawing) don't\ntofu out for fresh installs. agg uses fontconfig to resolve font families,\nso the font has to live in a directory fontconfig watches. The cleanest\ncross-platform path is to copy it into the user's standard font directory\non first use.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport os\nimport platform\nimport shutil\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\nBUNDLED_FONT_NAME = \"JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono\"\nBUNDLED_FONT_FILE = \"JetBrainsMonoNerdFontMono-Regular.ttf\"\n_FONT_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\n_BUNDLED_PATH = _FONT_DIR / BUNDLED_FONT_FILE\n\n\ndef _user_font_dir() -> Path:\n    if sys.platform == \"darwin\":\n        return Path.home() / \"Library\" / \"Fonts\"\n    if sys.platform.startswith(\"win\"):\n        return Path(os.environ.get(\"LOCALAPPDATA\", Path.home() / \"AppData/Local\")) / \"Microsoft/Windows/Fonts\"\n    return Path(os.environ.get(\"XDG_DATA_HOME\", Path.home() / \".local/share\")) / \"fonts\"\n\n\ndef _font_resolved_via_fontconfig(family: str) -> bool:\n    try:\n        out = subprocess.run(\n            [\"fc-match\", \"--format=%{family}\", family],\n            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=5,\n        )\n        # fc-match always returns success and falls back silently to a different\n        # family if the requested one isn't installed. So the only signal is\n        # whether the resolved family contains the requested name.\n        return out.returncode == 0 and family.lower() in out.stdout.lower()\n    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.SubprocessError):\n        return False\n\n\ndef _refresh_fontconfig_cache() -> None:\n    try:\n        subprocess.run([\"fc-cache\", \"-f\"], capture_output=True, timeout=30)\n    except (FileNotFoundError, subprocess.SubprocessError):\n        pass\n\n\n_ENSURE_DONE = False\n\n\ndef ensure_bundled_font_installed(*, verbose: bool = True) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Make the bundled Nerd Font discoverable by fontconfig.\n\n    Idempotent and cheap to call: bails out as soon as the font is already\n    resolvable. On first run, copies the bundled TTF into the platform's\n    user fonts directory and refreshes the fontconfig cache.\n\n    Returns True if the font is available after this call, False otherwise.\n    \"\"\"\n    global _ENSURE_DONE\n    if _ENSURE_DONE:\n        return True\n\n    if _font_resolved_via_fontconfig(BUNDLED_FONT_NAME):\n        _ENSURE_DONE = True\n        return True\n\n    if not _BUNDLED_PATH.exists():\n        if verbose:\n            print(\n                f\"[moirae] WARNING: bundled font missing at {_BUNDLED_PATH}; \"\n                f\"renders may show tofu boxes for Braille/symbol glyphs.\",\n                file=sys.stderr,\n            )\n        return False\n\n    target_dir = _user_font_dir()\n    target = target_dir / _BUNDLED_PATH.name\n    try:\n        target_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n        if not target.exists():\n            shutil.copy2(_BUNDLED_PATH, target)\n            if verbose:\n                print(\n                    f\"[moirae] Installed bundled Nerd Font to {target} \"\n                    f\"(needed for full glyph coverage in renders).\",\n                    file=sys.stderr,\n                )\n        _refresh_fontconfig_cache()\n    except Exception as exc:\n        if verbose:\n            print(\n                f\"[moirae] WARNING: could not install bundled Nerd Font \"\n                f\"to {target_dir}: {exc}. Renders may show tofu boxes for \"\n                f\"Braille/symbol glyphs. Manual install: copy \"\n                f\"{_BUNDLED_PATH} into your system fonts directory.\",\n                file=sys.stderr,\n            )\n        return False\n\n    if _font_resolved_via_fontconfig(BUNDLED_FONT_NAME):\n        _ENSURE_DONE = True\n        return True\n\n    if verbose:\n        print(\n            f\"[moirae] WARNING: bundled font copied to {target} but \"\n            f\"fontconfig still does not resolve '{BUNDLED_FONT_NAME}'. \"\n            f\"You may need to log out / log back in or run `fc-cache -f` \"\n            f\"manually.\",\n            file=sys.stderr,\n        )\n    return False\n"
}

Two compounding things, one is my fault:

**Answering your other questions:**

**"What even is that video?"** — when I dispatched the preview/smoke-test subagent earlier, it ran `python -m moirae fonts test` on its own as a smoke test of its own work, which auto-opened a tiny ~5-sec mp4 of glyphs. That's what you saw. It was the subagent verifying its build, not a render of your screenplay. The full `wan-animate-qa-aa` render kept going meanwhile.

**"How can you tell what good fonts is there?"** — three ways, increasing rigor:

```bash
# 1. List fonts that have Braille glyphs (U+2800–28FF)
fc-list :charset=2800-28ff family | sort -u

# 2. Confirm a specific font has it (returns the requested family if yes,
#    silently falls back to a different one if no — so check the output)
fc-match "JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono:charset=2800"

# 3. Use the smoke-test command the subagent is currently building:
python3 -m moirae fonts test --font "<name>"
```

The smoke command (when the subagent lands its push) is the clean answer — renders all the problematic glyphs in a 5-sec clip and you eyeball it.

**The Braille caduceus is now removed** from the screenplay — replaced with a box-drawn tagline:

```

║       on how to unlock open-source AI models.                                ║

```

Box-drawing chars are bulletproof — any monospace font has them. No Braille dependency. Auto-opens when render completes.

> AGENT

Good architectural question. Spent half the day fighting these — here's where the gremlins actually live, ranked by how likely they're causing the misalignment you're seeing:

### Top suspects

1. **Predictive midpoint at response_start** (**this is the one I'm fixing right now**). `_auto_track_keyframes` in `camera.py` emits a keyframe at `response_start` time targeted at the *predicted* Q+A midpoint — so the camera jumps DOWN the moment the response starts, before any response text has rendered. Result: question shifts up to top of viewport, then response slowly types into the middle. That's the "moves before the message arrives" feeling.

2. **No keyframes during response render.** Moirae emits keyframes at `user_start`, `user_end`, `response_start`. Then nothing until the next scene. So during a 12-line response that takes 5 seconds to type out, the camera is held at the predictive midpoint. If the response is long, the cursor walks off the bottom while the camera sits still.

3. **Cursor row tracked by `text.count("\n")`** in `scenes/__init__.py` — vulnerable to trailing newlines, lines that wrap at 200 cols (because nobody counts wraps), and content that uses `\r` instead of `\n`. The longer the screenplay, the more drift accumulates between Moirae's belief about cursor row and the terminal's actual row.

4. **Terminal scrolling vs `cursor_row` accounting.** When content exceeds 80 rows, the terminal buffer scrolls. Moirae's `cursor_row` tracker just keeps incrementing past 80; the auto_y math then divides by 80 and clamps to 1.0. So everything past row 80 maps to "viewport bottom", losing all granularity.

5. **Default keyframe at `t=0` with `y=0.34`** (magic number in `camera.py:167`). Any screenplay with no explicit camera at t=0 inherits this bias toward the top. If your first explicit keyframe is at t=1.5s (after banner), there's a visible interpolation from y=0.34 to whatever for the first 1.5s.

6. **`action: camera` reads y from `timing.markers["_y"]`** in `camera.py:137` — but I'm not sure those markers are populated from the YAML scene fields. Worth grepping. If they aren't, all `action: camera` directives silently default to (zoom=1.0, x=0.5, y=0.5) regardless of what you put in the YAML.

7. **`action: banner` doesn't track cursor per line.** It renders multi-line ASCII art via Rich but only emits ONE scene_timing. Subsequent scenes inherit a cursor_row that's roughly correct but not exactly tracked.

### What I'm doing right now

Fixing #1 + #2 in the same patch: instead of a predictive midpoint keyframe at response_start, emit a *tracking* keyframe at `response_end` with `duration = response_end_time − response_start_time`. The camera then pans smoothly from the user_end position to the response_end position over the actual response-render time. The active cursor stays roughly centered the whole way.

#3, #4, #6 are real but separate fixes. #5 is a config tweak. I'll note them as follow-ups after we ship today.

Now let me patch it.

```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/moirae/camera.py",
  "old_string": "def _auto_track_keyframes(\n    keyframes: List[CameraKeyframe],\n    cam,\n    timing,\n    total_rows: int,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit tracking keyframes at user_end and response_start.\"\"\"\n    # Follow cursor after submit\n    t = timing.markers.get(\"user_end\")\n    if t is not None:\n        auto = _resolve_auto_y(\"user_end\", timing, total_rows)\n        if auto is not None:\n            keyframes.append(CameraKeyframe(\n                t=t, zoom=cam.zoom, x=cam.x, y=auto,\n                duration=0.3, ease=\"ease-out\",\n            ))\n\n    # Center on Q+A midpoint when response appears\n    t = timing.markers.get(\"response_start\")\n    top = timing.markers.get(\"_cursor_user_start\")\n    bottom = timing.markers.get(\"_cursor_response_end\")\n    if t is not None and top is not None and bottom is not None:\n        midpoint = (top + bottom) / 2.0\n        y = min(midpoint / total_rows, 1.0)\n        keyframes.append(CameraKeyframe(\n            t=t, zoom=cam.zoom, x=cam.x, y=y,\n            duration=0.3, ease=\"ease-out\",\n        ))",
  "new_string": "def _auto_track_keyframes(\n    keyframes: List[CameraKeyframe],\n    cam,\n    timing,\n    total_rows: int,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Emit tracking keyframes that follow the cursor through the exchange.\n\n    Three keyframes per Q+A:\n      1. user_end  — pan to the cursor's row right after the user prompt is done.\n      2. response_start — hold (no jump). We deliberately do NOT pre-position\n         the camera at the predicted Q+A midpoint; that creates a visible\n         lead where the camera moves before the response actually renders.\n      3. response_end — pan smoothly to the cursor's row at response end,\n         with duration spanning the entire response render. The compositor\n         interpolates linearly through this window, so the active line\n         stays roughly under the viewport center as it gets typed.\n    \"\"\"\n    user_end_t = timing.markers.get(\"user_end\")\n    user_end_row = timing.markers.get(\"_cursor_user_end\")\n    response_start_t = timing.markers.get(\"response_start\")\n    response_end_t = timing.markers.get(\"response_end\")\n    response_end_row = timing.markers.get(\"_cursor_response_end\")\n\n    if user_end_t is not None and user_end_row is not None:\n        keyframes.append(CameraKeyframe(\n            t=user_end_t,\n            zoom=cam.zoom, x=cam.x,\n            y=min(user_end_row / total_rows, 1.0) if total_rows > 0 else 0.5,\n            duration=0.3, ease=\"ease-out\",\n        ))\n\n    if (\n        response_start_t is not None\n        and response_end_t is not None\n        and response_end_row is not None\n    ):\n        track_duration = max(response_end_t - response_start_t, 0.3)\n        keyframes.append(CameraKeyframe(\n            t=response_end_t,\n            zoom=cam.zoom, x=cam.x,\n            y=min(response_end_row / total_rows, 1.0) if total_rows > 0 else 0.5,\n            duration=track_duration,\n            ease=\"linear\",\n        ))"
}

## How ArtAgents handles video timeline + text + effects

There's a full timeline pipeline already. Two paths, depending on whether you want to compose by hand or visually edit.

### Option A — programmatic timeline + render

ArtAgents builds video as a **timeline JSON + assets JSON**, then renders it via Remotion. The pieces:

| Element kind | What's there today | Where it lives |
|---|---|---|
| **animations** | `fade`, `fade-up`, `scale-in`, `slide-left`, `slide-up`, `type-on` (typewriter text reveal) | `artagents/packs/builtin/<name>/` |
| **effects** | `text-card` (caption/title overlay) | same |
| **transitions** | `cross-fade`, `fade` (through black) | same |

The shape: a **timeline** is an ordered list of clips. Each clip references a media asset (the Moirae MP4 here) and can have **animations** (entrance/exit on the clip), **effects** (overlays like `text-card`), and **transitions** (between adjacent clips).

The render path:

```bash
# Inspect the schema each element accepts:
python3 -m artagents elements inspect text-card --json
python3 -m artagents elements inspect type-on --json

# Once you have a timeline.json + assets.json:
python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.render \
  --input timeline=path/to/timeline.json \
  --input assets=path/to/assets.json \
  --out out/composed.mp4
```

For your case: one clip of `wan-animate-qa-aa/video.mp4`, with a `text-card` effect at `t=0–3s` saying e.g. "Wan Animate — Banodoco knowledge dump". The Remotion composition picks up `text-card` and renders the overlay on top.

### Option B — open in Reigh (the visual editor)

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.open_in_reigh \
  --input timeline=runs/wan-animate-qa-aa/timeline.json \
  --input assets=runs/wan-animate-qa-aa/assets.json
```

Reigh is the visual editor app — opens the timeline in a UI where you drag clips, type text, position effects. Then re-render via the same pipeline.

### What's missing right now

The Moirae output today is just a bare `video.mp4` — no `timeline.json` + `assets.json` next to it. To use it via either path you need to wrap it. Two ways:

1. **Manual** — write a 20-line `timeline.json` referencing the MP4 + a `text-card` effect, save next to the video.
2. **Automated** — `builtin.iteration_prepare` already does this for hype-cut workflows. We could add a similar `external.moirae` post-step that emits the timeline + assets next to the MP4.

## Report

**Bug.** `show_response` printed the whole `Panel(Markdown(text))` in one tick, so `_cursor_response_start` and `_cursor_response_end` were emitted ~0ms apart. The auto-tracking camera then lerped slowly between cursor rows that had already teleported — content appeared, camera "caught up".

**Fix.** Render the panel into a recording `rich.Console`, capture styled ANSI via `export_text(styles=True)`, and replay line-by-line with `sys.stdout.write` + `time.sleep(line_delay)`. Each emitted line calls `ctx.newline(1)`, so `cursor_row` grows monotonically across the same window the camera interpolates over. All Rich styling (Panel border, Markdown bold, code blocks, syntax colors) is preserved exactly as before.

### Files changed
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/moirae/scenes/conversation.py` — new `show_response` streams panel rows; added `Console` import; `play_conversation` passes `scene.response_speed` (default 0.06).
- `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/moirae/schema.py` — added `ConversationScene.response_speed: Optional[float] = None`.

### Commit
- `8ab7caf` pushed to `origin/main` (fast-forward from `770510e`).

### Smoke transcript — first 10 lines of `python -m moirae fonts test`
```

### Visual confirmation of progressive render
Direct unit-style invocation of `show_response` on a 13-row Panel-with-Markdown: `cursor_row` advanced 0 → 13 incrementally, total elapsed **0.76s** at default `line_delay=0.05`. At the shipping default `0.06s/line`, a typical 12-line response reveals over **~0.72s**. This is the same window over which `auto_y` interpolates from `_cursor_response_start` to `_cursor_response_end`, so the cursor is now inside the lerp window for its entire duration. `--play` mode against `example.yaml` rendered all three responses progressively with full Rich styling intact (verified by inspecting the ANSI dump).

The full pipeline against `wan-animate-qa.yaml`: cast recorded successfully (200×120 grid, 43.66s wall time, ~3.5s longer than pre-fix from the added line delays — ~8%); GIF compositing was running but `agg` is extremely slow on long casts (unrelated to this fix), so I terminated it after confirming the upstream stages produced correct output. The cast is the source of truth for cursor markers, and it was clean.

### Panel rendering follow-up
One thing worth noting: the recording `Console` is created with `file=open("/dev/null", "w")` to keep `record=True` from also writing to a real stdout. Closing it in a `finally` is best-effort. Long-term, switching to `Console(file=io.StringIO())` would be slightly cleaner — same effect, no fd. Not worth a follow-up commit on its own, but worth knowing if anyone touches this path again.</result>

## Final report

### 1. Discovery findings

**Schemas** (authoritative: `remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-schema/typescript/src/schemas.ts`):

- `timeline.json` — `{theme, theme_overrides?, tracks: [{id, kind: visual|audio, label, ...}], clips: [TimelineClip]}`. Canvas resolution/fps comes from `theme_overrides.visual.canvas`.
- `assets.json` — `{"assets": {"&lt;id&gt;": {file?: path, url?, type?, resolution?, fps?, duration?}}}`. Renderer serves locals over HTTP from a common parent dir.
- `TimelineClip` — `{id, at (seconds), track, clipType, asset?, from/to, hold, text?, params?, effects?, x?, y?, width?, height?, entrance?, exit?, transition?}`.

**Example clip + overlay snippet:**
```json
{"id":"src","at":0,"track":"v1","clipType":"media","asset":"src","from":0,"to":49.5}
{"id":"cap1","at":3,"track":"ov","clipType":"text","hold":10,
 "effects":{"fade_in":0.4,"fade_out":0.4},
 "text":{"content":"search 1.2 million messages","fontSize":38,"color":"#ffffff","align":"right"},
 "params":{"anchor":"bottom-right","offsetX":80,"offsetY":140,"maxWidth":720,"weight":600}}
```

**Big finding**: the built-in `text-card` component is `() =&gt; null` — text rendering is delegated to a theme override that doesn't ship in this repo. Any timeline with `clipType: "text"` renders as nothing unless you fork the element. Notes at `/tmp/timeline-schema-notes.md`.

### 2. Files added/changed

- New (gitignored): `artagents/packs/local/elements/effects/text-card/{component.tsx,element.yaml}` (~190 lines TSX) — fork providing real DOM rendering with anchor positioning + fade in/out.
- New (gitignored): `runs/wan-animate-qa-aa-test/{timeline.json,assets.json,composed.mp4}`.
- Modified: `artagents/packs/_core/skill/SKILL.md` (via symlink `SKILL.md`) — added "Adding overlays to a rendered video" section (~70 lines).
- Modified + pushed: `/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Moirae/SKILL.md` — added cross-link to the ArtAgents recipe (commit `bd132ac`, pushed to `origin/main`).
- Notes: `/tmp/timeline-schema-notes.md`.

### 4. SKILL.md section added

Section title and headings:

### 5. Rough-edges list (worth fixing)

1. **`text-card` is a no-op stub** in the builtin pack. Anything that emits `clipType: "text"` (e.g. `cut.py` line 588) silently renders nothing unless a theme is active. Two paths forward: (a) ship a real default TextCard in the builtin pack, or (b) make the renderer fail loudly when an effect-id resolves to a `() =&gt; null` component without a theme override.
2. **`gen_effect_registry.py` writes to the wrong place by default.** It defaults to `WORKSPACE_ROOT/packages/timeline-composition/...`, but Remotion imports from `node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition/...`. The two are unrelated copies. The render path auto-runs the codegen but it doesn't actually update what gets bundled. Required workaround: `ARTAGENTS_TIMELINE_COMPOSITION_SRC=...node_modules/...` on every invocation. Either change the default to follow the install location, or have `render.run` pass that env var automatically.
3. **Webpack cache poisoning across runs.** After editing a forked element's `component.tsx`, the next render reuses `remotion/node_modules/.cache/webpack` and ignores the new source. Cost me 30 minutes. Fix: invalidate that cache when generated registries change.
4. **Track ordering is reversed silently.** `[...getVisualTracks(timeline)].reverse()` in `TimelineComposition.tsx` means overlay tracks listed second appear *behind* the source. There's no docstring or schema hint. Either name the field `tracks_back_to_front` or document it on the schema.
5. **Effect-component opacity not provided by the harness.** `useFadeOpacity` is only applied inside `VisualClip` (video/image). Effect components have to re-implement it. A `useClipOpacity(clip, fps)` hook re-exported from `@banodoco/timeline-composition` would save every effect author from this footgun.
6. **`element.yaml` schema for text-card** lists only `content`/`align` even though `clip.text` and `clip.params` actually accept many more fields (font, color, etc.) read by downstream renderers. Default schema should at least cover `TextClipData`.
7. **No fixture under `tests/fixtures/` covers a non-empty rendered timeline** — the only `hype.timeline.json` fixture has `clips: []`. Hard to learn the shape from tests; had to read `cut.py` instead.
8. **`builtin.render`'s declared `inputs` are all `required: false`** but `render` raises if `--timeline`/`--assets` are missing. Tighten the executor manifest.
9. **The CLI gateway** `python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.render` was suggested in the prompt but the script has its own argparse — I went straight to `python3 -m artagents.packs.builtin.render.run`. Worth verifying which is the intended public path.

### 6. Open decisions / things you may want to revisit

- The fade durations and 80px insets are taste calls — easy to tweak `params.offsetX/Y` and `effects.fade_in/out` in `runs/wan-animate-qa-aa-test/timeline.json` and re-render.
- Cap2/3/4 are long enough to wrap to two lines at the chosen `maxWidth`. If you'd rather one-line + smaller font, drop `fontSize` to ~28 or widen `maxWidth` past 1100.
- The forked TextCard lives in `artagents/packs/local/...` (gitignored). If we want this to be the real ArtAgents default, it should move into `artagents/packs/builtin/elements/effects/text-card/component.tsx` — but that's a write you'd need to approve given the staged-changes guardrail.</result>

The subagent found this MUCH harder than it should be. The headline finding:

### `text-card` is a no-op stub

Read this carefully — it's the kind of thing that loses afternoons:

> **The built-in `text-card` component is `() => null` — text rendering is delegated to a theme override that doesn't ship in this repo. Any timeline with `clipType: "text"` renders as nothing unless you fork the element.**

So `cut.py` line 588 emits `clipType: "text"` clips that silently render to **nothing** in the default pack. The agent had to fork `text-card` into `artagents/packs/local/elements/effects/text-card/component.tsx` (~190 lines TSX) just to get text on screen.

### The 9 rough edges worth fixing as follow-ups

1. **`text-card` no-op default** — ship a real default OR make the renderer fail loudly when `clipType: "text"` resolves to `() => null`. (Highest priority — this is a gotcha that wastes everyone's first attempt.)
2. **`gen_effect_registry.py` writes to wrong path** by default. Has to be overridden via `ARTAGENTS_TIMELINE_COMPOSITION_SRC=...node_modules/...` env var on every invocation.
3. **Webpack cache poisoning** — edits to forked components are ignored until you nuke `remotion/node_modules/.cache/webpack`. Cost the agent 30 min.

110	    // top/bottom/center: horizontally centred
111	    style.left = '50%';
112	    style.transform = style.transform
113	      ? 'translate(-50%, -50%)'
114	      : 'translateX(-50%)';
115	  }
116	  return style;
117	};
118	
119	const flexAlign = (align: 'left' | 'center' | 'right' | undefined): CSSProperties => {
120	  if (align === 'left') return {textAlign: 'left'};
121	  if (align === 'right') return {textAlign: 'right'};
122	  return {textAlign: 'center'};
123	};
124	
125	export default function TextCard(props: {
126	  clip: any;
127	  params: any;
128	  theme: unknown;
129	  fps: number;
130	}): ReactElement | null {
131	  const frame = useCurrentFrame();
132	  const {fps} = useVideoConfig();
133	  const clip: any = props.clip;
134	  const text: TextData = (clip.text ?? props.params ?? {}) as TextData;
135	  const card: CardParams = (clip.params ?? {}) as CardParams;
136	
137	  const content = text.content ?? '';
138	  if (!content) return null;
139	
140	  const sourceDuration =
141	    typeof clip.hold === 'number'
142	      ? clip.hold
143	      : (clip.to ?? 0) - (clip.from ?? 0);
144	  const speed = clip.speed ?? 1;
145	  const durationFrames = Math.max(1, Math.round((sourceDuration / speed) * fps));
146	  const opacity = fadeOpacity(clip.effects, frame, durationFrames, fps);
147	
148	  const align = text.align ?? 'left';
149	
150	  // Manual x/y/width/height wins over anchor mode.
151	  const useManual =
152	    clip.x !== undefined || clip.y !== undefined ||
153	    clip.width !== undefined || clip.height !== undefined;
154	
155	  const anchor: Anchor = card.anchor ?? 'center';
156	  const offsetX = card.offsetX ?? 0;
157	  const offsetY = card.offsetY ?? 0;
158	
159	  const positionStyle: CSSProperties = useManual
160	    ? {
161	        position: 'absolute',
162	        left: clip.x,
163	        top: clip.y,
164	        width: clip.width,
165	        height: clip.height,
166	      }
167	    : anchorPosition(anchor, offsetX, offsetY);
168	
169	  const containerStyle: CSSProperties = {
170	    ...positionStyle,
171	    maxWidth: card.maxWidth,
172	    opacity,
173	    pointerEvents: 'none',
174	    boxSizing: 'border-box',
175	  };
176	
177	  const cardStyle: CSSProperties = {
178	    background: card.background,
179	    padding: card.padding,
180	    borderRadius: card.borderRadius,
181	    color: text.color ?? '#ffffff',
182	    fontFamily: text.fontFamily ?? 'Inter, system-ui, sans-serif',
183	    fontSize: text.fontSize ?? 36,
184	    fontWeight: card.weight ?? (text.bold ? 700 : 500),
185	    fontStyle: text.italic ? 'italic' : 'normal',
186	    lineHeight: card.lineHeight ?? 1.25,
187	    letterSpacing: card.letterSpacing,
188	    textShadow: card.textShadow ?? '0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.6)',
189	    ...flexAlign(align),
190	    whiteSpace: 'pre-wrap',
191	    wordBreak: 'break-word',
192	  };
193	
194	  return (
195	    <div style={containerStyle}>
196	      <div style={cardStyle}>{content}</div>
197	    </div>
198	  );
199	}

> AGENT

Source render `bxmc5sh8y` running. Will wait for it, then composite.

To explain the centering bug — it's not a calc, it's a CSS gotcha:

`anchor: 'center'` produces `transform: translate(-50%, -50%)` which is what actually centers the panel (the panel's anchor point is its top-left corner; the translate shifts it back by half its width/height). Then the slide-in animation also wants to set `transform: translateY(20px)`. CSS `transform` is a single property — the second assignment **overwrites** the first. So whenever the slide animation was active, the centering vanished and the panel sat with its top-left corner at the screen's center, looking right-aligned.

Fix: combine them — `transform: 'translate(-50%, -50%) translateY(20px)'`. Now both apply.

To answer your question: **the timeline data is flat**, not nested. Each clip is its own JSON object in `clips: []`, with its own `text`, `params`, `effects`, etc. Nothing is "layered into" anything else at the data level. The bug wasn't data nesting — it was a CSS-side property collision: `transform` is a single CSS string, and my code was overwriting the centering `translate(-50%, -50%)` with the slide animation's `translateY(...)`. Last write wins, so centering vanished. The fix concatenates both into one `transform` string, which CSS applies as a sequence.

The renderable timeline is a real flat structure — every clip is independently positioned, animated, and styled. They overlap visually only because of their `at`/`hold` timing windows and z-order (later clips in the array render on top within a track).

Will fire `open` automatically when both renders finish.

> AGENT

**Found the root cause** — and it's one bug that explains both problems.

In the component:

```ts
const cardWrapperStyle: CSSProperties = {
  background: card.background,
  padding: card.padding,                         // "48px 72px 44px 72px"
  paddingLeft: card.spriteSpace ? ... : undefined,   // ← BUG
  ...
};
```

When `spriteSpace` isn't set, this evaluates to `paddingLeft: undefined`. React applies that as a property override — it **wipes the left value** that the `padding` shorthand had just set. So padding-left was effectively 0, and padding-right was still 72px. Asymmetric padding → all text shifted left → "centered text" appearing not in the middle of the card → captions with "no left buffer space."

Same bug for both issues — title cards AND captions. One fix.

> TOOL

tool_use Edit
```json
{
  "replace_all": false,
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/reigh-workspace/ArtAgents/artagents/packs/local/elements/effects/text-card/component.tsx",
  "old_string": "  // Card wrapper holds BOTH subtitle and content so they read as a single\n  // panel against the source video underneath.\n  const cardWrapperStyle: CSSProperties = {\n    background: card.background,\n    padding: card.padding,\n    paddingLeft: card.spriteSpace\n      ? (typeof card.padding === 'number' ? card.padding : 28) + card.spriteSpace\n      : undefined,\n    borderRadius: card.borderRadius,\n    border: card.border,\n    borderLeft: card.borderLeft,\n    backdropFilter: card.backdropFilter,\n    WebkitBackdropFilter: card.backdropFilter,\n    boxShadow: card.boxShadow,\n    boxSizing: 'border-box',\n    display: 'inline-block',\n    position: 'relative',\n  };",
  "new_string": "  // Card wrapper holds BOTH subtitle and content so they read as a single\n  // panel against the source video underneath.\n  const cardWrapperStyle: CSSProperties = {\n    background: card.background,\n    padding: card.padding,\n    borderRadius: card.borderRadius,\n    border: card.border,\n    borderLeft: card.borderLeft,\n    backdropFilter: card.backdropFilter,\n    WebkitBackdropFilter: card.backdropFilter,\n    boxShadow: card.boxShadow,\n    boxSizing: 'border-box',\n    display: 'inline-block',\n    position: 'relative',\n  };\n  // Only override paddingLeft when sprite space is requested. Setting\n  // `paddingLeft: undefined` inline alongside the `padding` shorthand\n  // wipes the left value React just set — that was making every panel\n  // render with padding-left 0 and padding-right intact, so all text\n  // looked nudged to the left of its container.\n  if (card.spriteSpace) {\n    cardWrapperStyle.paddingLeft =\n      (typeof card.padding === 'number' ? card.padding : 28) + card.spriteSpace;\n  }"
}

**To answer the "fundamental" question**: yes, the layout *should* be simple. The reason it's been hard is that the inline-block + padding shorthand + conditional `paddingLeft: undefined` interaction was silently corrupting the box model. Once you have one bad pixel boundary in the chain, everything downstream looks "almost centered" but slightly off — and visually, your eye reads that as "not centered at all." It wasn't 5 different bugs; it was one bug compounding across every panel that uses the component.

# Sprite Sheet Executor

Use `builtin.sprite_sheet` to create animation sprite sheets and sliced frame
previews from a subject plus animation description.

Dry-run or inspect first:

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors inspect builtin.sprite_sheet
python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.sprite_sheet --out runs/sprites/wave --input animation=wave --input subject="neon courier" --dry-run
```

Requires image API credentials for generation and `ffmpeg` for slicing/preview
exports.

## Outputs

Expected files include:

- `{out}/sprite_manifest.json`
- `{out}/sprite_sheet.png`
- `{out}/sprite_sheet_alpha.png`
- `{out}/frames/frame_001.png` and sibling frame PNGs
- `{out}/sprite_preview.mp4`
- `{out}/web/sprite_sheet.webp` and web preview outputs when web export is enabled

Safety-edge warnings mean one or more sliced frames touch the configured edge
margin. Treat that as a soft QA warning for prototypes and a prompt/layout retry
signal for production sprites.

# Generate Image Executor

Use `builtin.generate_image` when an agent needs bitmap image assets for timelines,
collages, pitch frames, visual treatments, or fallback art packs.

This executor wraps `artagents.packs.builtin.generate_image.run` and expects a prompt file. Put one
prompt per line, or provide a JSON/JSONL list accepted by the underlying CLI.

## Commands

Inspect:

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors inspect builtin.generate_image
```

Dry-run:

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.generate_image \
  --out runs/example-images \
  --input prompts_file=runs/example-images/prompts.txt \
  --dry-run
```

Run:

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.generate_image \
  --out runs/example-images \
  --input prompts_file=runs/example-images/prompts.txt
```

## Outputs

- Images are written under `{out}/images`.
- The generation manifest is written to `{out}/manifest.json`.

## Presets

Pass `--preset <name>` to use a canned prompt and behaviour bundle. Currently:

- `saint-peter-of-banodoco` — onboarding portrait of the maker as Saint Peter
  of Banodoco; opens the rendered image after writing it (use `--no-open` to
  skip). Run directly via the `run.py` entrypoint, since the executor manifest
  command pipes a prompt file rather than a preset:

  ```bash
  python3 -m artagents.packs.builtin.generate_image.run \
    --preset saint-peter-of-banodoco \
    --out-dir runs/first-rite/images \
    --manifest runs/first-rite/manifest.json \
    --force
  ```

  Add `--dry-run` to print the planned API call without spending tokens.

## Requirements

Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment or a supported local env file.

If one prompt is rejected by the image API, the current underlying CLI stops at
that failure. For batch work, prefer smaller prompt files so a single blocked
prompt does not waste earlier planning.
```

# Generate Image Executor

Use `builtin.generate_image` when an agent needs bitmap image assets for timelines,
collages, pitch frames, visual treatments, or fallback art packs.

This executor wraps `artagents.packs.builtin.generate_image.run` and expects a prompt file. Put one
prompt per line, or provide a JSON/JSONL list accepted by the underlying CLI.

## Commands

Inspect:

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors inspect builtin.generate_image
```

Dry-run:

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.generate_image \
  --out runs/example-images \
  --input prompts_file=runs/example-images/prompts.txt \
  --dry-run
```

Run:

```bash
python3 -m artagents executors run builtin.generate_image \
  --out runs/example-images \
  --input prompts_file=runs/example-images/prompts.txt
```

## Outputs

- Images are written under `{out}/images`.
- The generation manifest is written to `{out}/manifest.json`.

## Presets

Pass `--preset <name>` to use a canned prompt and behaviour bundle. Currently:

- `saint-peter-of-banodoco` — onboarding portrait of the maker as Saint Peter
  of Banodoco; opens the rendered image after writing it (use `--no-open` to
  skip). Run directly via the `run.py` entrypoint, since the executor manifest
  command pipes a prompt file rather than a preset:

  ```bash
  python3 -m artagents.packs.builtin.generate_image.run \
    --preset saint-peter-of-banodoco \
    --out-dir runs/first-rite/images \
    --manifest runs/first-rite/manifest.json \
    --force
  ```

  Add `--dry-run` to print the planned API call without spending tokens.

## Requirements

Requires `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment or a supported local env file.

If one prompt is rejected by the image API, the current underlying CLI stops at
that failure. For batch work, prefer smaller prompt files so a single blocked
prompt does not waste earlier planning.

# GPT Image API Skill

Use this skill when the task should call OpenAI's Image API directly instead of the built-in image tool.

The canonical Codex copy is:

```bash
${CODEX_HOME:-$HOME/.codex}/skills/.system/gpt-image
```

This Claude copy mirrors the same workflow and script:

```bash
python "$HOME/.claude/skills/gpt-image/scripts/gpt_image.py" generate \
  --prompt "A clean editorial product photo of a ceramic mug" \
  --n 2 \
  --size 1024x1024 \
  --quality medium \
  --output-format png \
  --out-dir output/gpt-image
```

## Current API Notes

Official docs checked on 2026-04-30:

- Image generation endpoint: `POST /v1/images/generations`.
- Latest GPT Image model in the guide: `gpt-image-2`.
- Direct generation supports `prompt`, `model`, `n`, `size`, `quality`, `output_format`, `output_compression`, `background`, and `moderation`.
- `gpt-image-2` accepts custom `WIDTHxHEIGHT` sizes when both edges are multiples of 16, max edge is <= 3840px, aspect ratio is <= 3:1, and total pixels are 655,360 to 8,294,400.
- Popular sizes include `1024x1024`, `1536x1024`, `1024x1536`, `2048x2048`, `2048x1152`, `3840x2160`, `2160x3840`, and `auto`.
- `quality`: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `auto`.
- `output_format`: `png`, `jpeg`, or `webp`; `output_compression` applies to JPEG/WebP.
- `moderation`: `auto` or `low`.
- `gpt-image-2` does not support transparent backgrounds.

Sources:

- https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/image-generation
- https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/images

## Prompt Lists

Use `--prompt` repeatedly or pass `--prompts-file`.

Supported prompt files:

- Plain text: one prompt per non-empty line.
- JSON array: `["prompt one", {"prompt": "prompt two", "n": 3, "size": "1536x1024"}]`
- JSONL: one string or object per line.

## API Key Handling

Never hardcode or print the API key. The script resolves `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment, any explicit `--env-file`, the Codex skill's `env-files.txt` registry, then common local env files including `.env` in the current directory or parents, `$HOME/.codex/.env`, `$HOME/.claude/.env`, and `$HOME/.hermes/.env`.

Confirmed across all three layers — **no grid mode exists**:

- `builtin.generate_image` (ArtAgents) flags: `--prompt`, `--prompts-file`, `--preset`, `--model`, `--n`, `--size`, `--quality`, `--output-format`, `--output-compression`, `--background`, `--moderation`. No grid.

- The OpenAI Image API itself only takes `prompt + n + size + quality + …`. No "render variants in a grid" API.

The closest thing the curated imagegen skill mentions is **prompt-engineering** a single image to look like a grid (`"4-panel comic"`, `"3×3 grid of 9 styles"` etc.). That's what you'd be remembering — it's a prompting pattern, not an SDK feature.

Two real options for you:

**A.** Keep the 9 separate generations going (in flight now), stitch with PIL/ffmpeg after — each cell is full-resolution + individually re-rollable. Best for quality + iteration.

**B.** Cancel and write ONE prompt asking GPT Image to draw a 3×3 panel of 9 styles in a single image. ~9× faster + 1 API call. But each cell is ~340×340 px so detail suffers, and if one cell is bad you have to re-roll the whole thing.

Honestly for "show me 9 sprite variants of this guy with enough detail to recognize him" → A is the right call. Want me to also kick off B in parallel as a fast preview while A finishes?

> AGENT

Real question, worth pausing on. Looking back honestly at the friction in this session:

### What stumbled and shouldn't have

**Silent / fast-fail issues that cost iteration time:**

1. Both sprite generations just now reported `exit 0` while actually erroring (`ModuleNotFoundError` first, then `Grid 4x2 at 256x256 violates gpt-image-2 size limits`). I only caught it because I peeked at the task output. The script returns non-zero, but the bash pipe through `tail` masked it. **No structural assertion that "did the artifact actually land?"**

2. The `gpt-image-2` size minimum (655,360 px) isn't surfaced anywhere in `sprite_sheet`'s STAGE.md, schema, or default flag interactions. Default `frame-width=256, frame-height=256` with default grid silently produces an out-of-spec request. **The default config doesn't satisfy its own runtime constraint.**

3. Earlier today: `text-card` was `() => null` by default. `gen_effect_registry.py` writes to the wrong path by default. `padding shorthand + paddingLeft: undefined wipes the left value` by default. **Every "default" we hit was technically valid in isolation but broken at the seams.**

4. Webpack cache poisoning — every component edit needed a manual `rm -rf .cache/webpack`. **No invalidation on TSX edits.**

5. JSON schema rejected `text.subtitle` silently — the previous render was kept and the `composed.mp4` mtime didn't change. I didn't notice until I diffed mtimes.

### The pattern under all of those

ArtAgents today treats each layer (executor manifest, generator script, schema, component, renderer, cwd) as **independently evolving**. But they form a tight pipeline where **one layer's default is the next layer's implicit dependency**, and that dependency isn't named anywhere. When it drifts, the failure surfaces at the end of a 5-10 minute render — visually — and you spend hours bisecting which layer drifted.

Concretely, the structural issues I'd file as work:

| Issue | Concrete fix |
|---|---|
| Wrappers swallow errors via `2>&1 \| tail` and report exit 0 | Wrappers verify expected output files exist + are non-trivial size before declaring success. Bash pipelines should `set -o pipefail`. |
| Default config violates runtime constraints | Add validation in `build_parser` / manifest load that rejects defaults that can't actually run (e.g. sprite_sheet should refuse a grid below GPT-Image min) |
| Schema-vs-component drift | Move schema authoring into the component file (TS-first) or generate the JSON Schema from the TS interface. Right now they're hand-edited in two places and diverge. |
| Iteration time = full pipeline | A `live` mode that watches timeline.json + component.tsx, re-bundles only what changed, regenerates a single still frame in <5s. Today there's nothing between "preview the first 8 sec at full slowness" and "full render." |
| No fixture for non-trivial cases | The only `timeline.json` fixture is `hype.timeline.json` with `clips: []`. New devs (and agents) learn the shape by reading `cut.py`. **One realistic fixture would have prevented half my mistakes today.** |
| cwd matters silently | Every wrapper either auto-cd's to its package root, or refuses to run with a clear error pointing at the right cwd |
| Webpack cache stale | Hash relevant source dirs and bust the cache when they change |

### The deepest one

**No fast feedback loop.** Every visual decision today went through asciinema-recording (real time) → agg (2-3 min) → ffmpeg with per-frame Python composite (1-3 min) → ffprobe / open / look. Even the existing `preview` command renders the full pipeline and then trims the mp4. With a feedback loop measured in minutes, *any* off-by-one drift compounds because you can't iterate on it. With a feedback loop measured in seconds, the same drift is a 30-second annoyance.

If I had to point at one structural fix that'd dominate the rest: **build a "render this single frame at this timestamp against this timeline JSON" hot-reload command that finishes in under 2 seconds.** That alone turns the next 10 sessions like today into 10 minutes each instead of 5 hours.

Both sprite renders are still in flight (`bzd6pljjy` jiggle, `bwi2zgz6j` twerk) at the corrected 512×512 size. Will report when they land.

You're right to push back. Honest answer:

**There IS half a tool — but not a complete one.** ArtAgents has:
- ✅ A sprite generator (`builtin.sprite_sheet`) that outputs `sprite_preview.mp4` (already animated), sprite_sheet.png, individual frames, and a manifest
- ✅ A timeline that supports `clipType: "media"` (loads any video)
- ✅ Manual `x/y/width/height` positioning for any clip

**What's missing:** there's no element / effect / clipType that connects "I generated a sprite via builtin.sprite_sheet" to "play that sprite inside a card overlay." `text-card` doesn't know about sprites; the `animations/` elements (fade, slide, scale-in, type-on) are entrance/exit wrappers — not frame-cycling players. So I was about to roll my own CSS background-position cycling because the seam between the two halves doesn't exist.

The right answer is to **just use `sprite_preview.mp4` as a positioned media clip on the timeline** — no new code:

```json
{
  "id": "hive-sprite",
  "at": 0,
  "track": "ov",
  "clipType": "media",
  "asset": "hive-sprite",
  "from": 0,
  "to": 4,
  "x": 912, "y": 312,
  "width": 96, "height": 96,
  "loop": true
}
```

Plus `assets.json`: `"hive-sprite": {"file": "jiggle.mp4"}`. That uses the existing media path, the existing positioning, and the existing renderer — zero new component code. The only "trick" is positioning it where the title card's black square is.

The structural gap is real and worth filing as a follow-up: a small `sprite-player` element (or a `topSpriteVideo` field on text-card) that takes a sprite_preview.mp4 URL and renders it inside its parent card. ~30 lines. After that, the workflow is: `sprite_sheet` → drop the output mp4 path into a card → done.

- (b) Build the `topSpriteVideo` field on text-card properly so future cards can do this without manual positioning. ~15 min, gets us a real primitive.

> AGENT

Render `bww89hho2` in flight.

The architectural change that closed the seam:

```diff
- return <EffectComponent clip={clip} params={...} theme={theme} fps={fps} />;
+ const assetEntry = getAssetEntry(clip, assets);
+ return <EffectComponent clip={clip} params={...} theme={theme} fps={fps} assetEntry={assetEntry} />;
```

Effect components now receive the same `assetEntry` that `VisualClip` does. `text-card` reads it and renders `<OffthreadVideo>` (for `.mp4`) or `<Img>` (for static images) instead of the black square — sniffed from the URL extension. So **any future effect component can use the standard `clip.asset` mechanism for sprites/images** without needing parallel asset-resolution code.

Wiring:
- `assets.json`: `jiggle-sprite → jiggle.mp4`, `twerk-sprite → twerk.mp4`
- `title-start`: `clip.asset: "jiggle-sprite"` → his idle dance plays above "Hive Mind" at the start
- `title-end`: `clip.asset: "twerk-sprite"` → he twerks above "Hive Mind" at the end

Auto-opens.

The change to `node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition/...` is upstream — worth noting as a follow-up to PR into the timeline-composition package so this isn't lost on `npm install`.

  "content": "\"\"\"Search YouTube for a query and download the top hit's audio as MP3.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport shutil\nimport subprocess\nimport sys\nfrom pathlib import Path\n\n\ndef _die(msg: str, code: int = 2) -> int:\n    print(f\"Error: {msg}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    return code\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)\n    parser.add_argument(\"--query\", required=True, help=\"YouTube search query.\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--out\",\n        required=True,\n        type=Path,\n        help=\"Output path. .mp3 extension is appended if missing.\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--audio-format\",\n        default=\"mp3\",\n        help=\"Audio format passed to yt-dlp --audio-format.\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--audio-quality\",\n        default=\"0\",\n        help=\"yt-dlp --audio-quality (0 = best for VBR).\",\n    )\n    args = parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n    if not shutil.which(\"yt-dlp\"):\n        return _die(\"yt-dlp not found on PATH. Install via `pip install yt-dlp`.\")\n    if not shutil.which(\"ffmpeg\"):\n        return _die(\"ffmpeg not found on PATH. yt-dlp needs it to extract audio.\")\n\n    out = args.out\n    if out.suffix == \"\":\n        out = out.with_suffix(f\".{args.audio_format}\")\n    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n\n    # yt-dlp's --output template controls the final filename. We want the\n    # extension to match args.audio_format so the post-processed file lands\n    # at the path our manifest declares as the output.\n    output_template = str(out.with_suffix(f\".%(ext)s\"))\n\n    cmd = [\n        \"yt-dlp\",\n        \"--no-warnings\",\n        \"--extract-audio\",\n        f\"--audio-format={args.audio_format}\",\n        f\"--audio-quality={args.audio_quality}\",\n        \"--output\",\n        output_template,\n        f\"ytsearch1:{args.query}\",\n    ]\n    print(f\"[youtube_audio] {' '.join(cmd)}\", file=sys.stderr)\n    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, capture_output=True, text=True)\n    if proc.returncode != 0:\n        sys.stderr.write(proc.stdout)\n        sys.stderr.write(proc.stderr)\n        return _die(f\"yt-dlp failed (exit {proc.returncode})\", proc.returncode)\n\n    if not out.exists():\n        return _die(\n            f\"yt-dlp returned success but expected output {out} is missing. \"\n            \"stdout:\\n\" + proc.stdout + \"\\nstderr:\\n\" + proc.stderr,\n            3,\n        )\n\n    print(f\"Downloaded: {out} ({out.stat().st_size:,} bytes)\", file=sys.stderr)\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(main())\n"
}

  "content": "---\nname: youtube_audio\ndescription: Search YouTube for a query and download the top hit's audio as MP3 via yt-dlp.\n---\n\n# YouTube Audio Executor\n\nUse `builtin.youtube_audio` to source background tracks for video composites\nwithout leaving the ArtAgents CLI. Wraps `yt-dlp`'s `ytsearch1:` selector\nplus `--extract-audio` so you give it a free-text query and get an MP3.\n\n## Quick reference\n\n```bash\npython3 -m artagents executors run builtin.youtube_audio \\\n  --input query=\"Moby Extreme Ways official audio\" \\\n  --out runs/audio/extreme-ways\n```\n\nOutput is `runs/audio/extreme-ways.mp3` (the executor appends `.mp3`\nautomatically when no extension is given).\n\n## Inputs\n\n| name  | type   | description |\n|-------|--------|-------------|\n| query | string | Free-text YouTube search query — top result's audio is downloaded. |\n\n## Outputs\n\n| name  | type | description |\n|-------|------|-------------|\n| audio | file | MP3 audio extracted from the top YouTube result. |\n\n## Requirements\n\n- `yt-dlp` on `PATH` (`pip install yt-dlp` or `brew install yt-dlp`)\n- `ffmpeg` on `PATH` (yt-dlp uses it for the audio-format conversion)\n\nThe executor checks both binaries at start and exits with a clear error\nif either is missing.\n\n## Composing with the rest of the pipeline\n\nMost useful as a one-shot before a render:\n\n```bash\n# 1. Download a track\npython3 -m artagents executors run builtin.youtube_audio \\\n  --input query=\"lo-fi study beat\" --out runs/audio/lofi\n\n# 2. Mux it under a rendered composite (start at 4s, fade out last 2.5s)\nffmpeg -y -i composed.mp4 -i runs/audio/lofi.mp3 \\\n  -filter_complex \"[1:a]atrim=0:DURATION,asetpts=PTS-STARTPTS,adelay=4000|4000,afade=t=out:st=FADE_START:d=2.5[a]\" \\\n  -map 0:v -map \"[a]\" -c:v copy -c:a aac -b:a 192k composed_with_music.mp4\n```\n\nWhere `DURATION = video_duration - 4` and `FADE_START = video_duration - 2.5`.\n\n## Caveats\n\n- **Respect YouTube's terms of service and copyright** — only download\n  material you have rights to use (your own uploads, Creative Commons\n  tracks, royalty-free libraries, music you license, etc.).\n- The top search hit is what you get; for a specific track it's worth\n  including the artist name and the word \"audio\" or \"official\" in the\n  query to avoid live performances and long-tail uploads.\n- Network is required at runtime. The cache mode is `none` so re-runs\n  always hit yt-dlp; if you need caching, write to a stable `--out` path\n  and check existence yourself before invoking.\n- `yt-dlp` versions drift quickly; if a download fails, run\n  `pip install -U yt-dlp` first.\n"
}

Two answers + audit:

**Audit of "everywhere in the video"** — `grep -nE "banodoco-search|discord-search"` against both `examples/wan-animate-qa.yaml` and `runs/wan-animate-qa-aa-test/timeline.json` came back empty. So:

- ✅ Screenplay first user prompt: `/hivemind` (was `/banodoco-search`)
- ✅ Title card start content: `Hivemind`
- ✅ Title card end content: `Hivemind`
- ✅ Title card CTA URL: `↗ github.com/banodoco/hivemind`
- ✅ End card CTA URL: same
- ✅ Persistent bottom-right CTA strip URL: same

The word "Banodoco" still appears in the agent's reply text (e.g. "the Banodoco community") — but that's the org name, not the skill, and you asked me to rename the skill, not the org. I left those alone. Say if you want them changed too.

**Timeline editing** — pretty easy but un-tooled.

How I'm doing it now: hand-rolled `python3 -c "import json; ..."` blocks that read `timeline.json`, mutate, and write back. Works fine for ~10-clip timelines. Nothing wrong with it but there's no domain-aware CLI like `artagents timeline set --clip cta-strip params.ctaText "..."`.

What does exist:
- `artagents/core/timeline.py` — Python module with timeline load/serialize helpers (`Timeline.load`, `Timeline.for_render`).
- `builtin.cut` — generates timelines from a hype workflow but doesn't edit existing ones.
- The Reigh app — the visual timeline editor (the canonical editing surface).

What's missing: a `timeline edit` / `timeline patch` CLI for scripted JSON tweaks. That'd be a real DX win for any kind of "rename / re-time / restyle" pass — same family of fixes as the DX cleanup megaplan we ran earlier.

**Tracks** — currently everything overlay is on **one** track (`ov`). Just two tracks total:

```
"tracks": [
  {"id": "ov", "kind": "visual", "label": "Overlays"},  // title cards, captions, CTA strip, blur, all on this
  {"id": "v1", "kind": "visual", "label": "Source"}     // the Moirae video
]
```

Within a track, render order is JSON-array order (later = on top). So the only z-control I have is the `clips: []` array order, which is why I had to put `outro-blur` BEFORE `title-end` in the array (so the title card renders on top of the blur).

A cleaner setup would split into named tracks: `branding` (title/end cards), `captions` (cap1–4), `cta` (the persistent strip), `fx` (the blur), `source` (Moirae). Each track's z-order is defined once instead of by array position. The `track-listing-reverse` quirk we discovered earlier (rough-edge #4 in the DX audit) makes this trickier than it should be — the megaplan should fix it.

Source render `bjx143h5w` is in flight; once it lands I'll re-render the composite + re-mux. Then I'll update the GitHub repo (rename `discord-search` references → `hivemind`).

> DEVELOPER

And for creating new tracks, I think that would be way cleaner but can you try to understand why you didn't do this? And is it an issue with the kind of timeline, the skill associated with the timeline or not loading that? Or you're not having tools to add stuff to the timeline. What's fundamentally the issue here?

> AGENT

Honest answer: **none of those is the real cause** — the skill loads fine, the schema supports multiple tracks, the tooling could be better but isn't blocking. The real cause is structural, and it's the same pattern we hit twice before this session.

Ranked by how much each contributed:

1. **No fixture / no canonical example.** The only timeline fixture in the repo is `hype.timeline.json` with `clips: []`. The discovery agent's brief showed me a single-overlay-track shape. I read that as "this is how it's done" and copied it. **First-time agents (and humans) learn the design pattern from the example, not from the schema.** The skill says "tracks is an array of TrackDefinition" — that's the wire format. It doesn't say "use one track per concern: branding / captions / fx / source." Different things.

2. **The `getVisualTracks(...).reverse()` quirk silently penalizes more tracks.** Tracks listed second render behind tracks listed first. With one track, I had ONE z-order rule (array position). With four tracks, I'd have to remember the reverse rule + within-track array order. That's two layers of silent ordering. The cost-benefit math at iteration speed pointed at "stick with one track, manage z via clip order in the array." That's exactly the wrong incentive — the DX is steering me toward fragile timelines.

3. **No `timeline track add` / no track template.** Adding a track means hand-editing JSON. Adding a clip is also hand-editing JSON. Adding a clip is one entry; adding a track + the clip = two entries + getting the reverse-order right. Path of least resistance wins. A `timeline patch` CLI (rough-edge follow-up territory) would flip this.

4. **The skill doc teaches schema, not design.** `_core/skill/SKILL.md` and `docs/skills-install.md` cover "what fields exist." They don't cover "what makes a timeline maintainable" — track-per-concern, clip-naming conventions, when to break up an overlay layer. **Agents hit the schema right and produce structurally fragile timelines.**

5. **No timeline linter.** Nothing flags "you have 8+ overlay clips on one track; consider splitting." A linter would have nudged me at clip 5.

**The deepest pattern** — same one as the morning's rough-edges audit and the "why was Moirae so painful" diagnostic:

ArtAgents has a clean wire format (manifests, schemas, JSON timelines) but **the design conventions that turn the wire format into maintainable artifacts live nowhere**. Each agent (Claude, Codex, you, me) reinvents them on first contact, copying whatever the nearest existing example shows. When the example is `clips: []` or a one-track demo, the cargo cult propagates.

The fix isn't more tooling. It's the timeline DX cleanup we already filed (rough-edge #7 in the audit: "non-trivial timeline fixture") plus a short "design conventions" section in the SKILL.md that says the obvious things: branding gets its own track, captions get their own, the persistent CTA gets its own. **One paragraph would have prevented this.**

Want me to add that to the timeline DX cleanup brief as an explicit deliverable, so when the megaplan executor lands the change there's a fixture and a one-paragraph design-conventions section?

42	/** Normalize data so each point sums to exactly 100% */
43	function normalizeData(data: ModelTrend[]): ModelTrend[] {
44	  return data.map((point) => {
45	    const total = MODEL_KEYS.reduce((sum, key) => sum + (point[key as keyof ModelTrend] as number || 0), 0);
46	    if (total === 0 || Math.abs(total - 100) < 0.01) return point;
47	
48	    const normalized: Record<string, string | number> = { ...point };
49	    MODEL_KEYS.forEach((key) => {
50	      normalized[key] = ((point[key as keyof ModelTrend] as number) || 0) * (100 / total);
51	    });
52	    return normalized as unknown as ModelTrend;
53	  });
54	}

56	/** Ease-out cubic: starts fast, slows at end */
57	function getStepDuration(progress: number): number {
58	  const eased = 1 - Math.pow(1 - progress, 3);

291	/** Custom animated legend that shows models in order of appearance */
292	const AnimatedLegend: React.FC<{
293	  visibleModels: Set<string>;
294	  firstAppearances: Record<string, number>;
295	}> = ({ visibleModels, firstAppearances }) => {
296	  // Sort models by appearance frame, then filter to only visible ones
297	  const sortedVisibleModels = Object.entries(MODEL_COLORS)
298	    .filter(([key]) => visibleModels.has(key))
299	    .sort((a, b) => (firstAppearances[a[0]] ?? 0) - (firstAppearances[b[0]] ?? 0));
300	
301	  return (
302	    <div className="flex flex-wrap justify-center items-center gap-x-2 gap-y-1 sm:gap-x-3 px-2 sm:px-4 min-h-[32px]">
303	      <AnimatePresence mode="popLayout">
304	        {sortedVisibleModels.map(([key, { stroke, name }]) => (
305	          <LegendItem key={key} modelKey={key} stroke={stroke} name={name} />
306	        ))}
307	      </AnimatePresence>
308	    </div>
309	  );
310	};

313	
314	const ModelTrends: React.FC<ModelTrendsProps> = ({ data }) => {
315	  const sectionRef = useRef<HTMLElement>(null);
316	  const normalizedData = useMemo(() => normalizeData(data), [data]);
317	  const totalFrames = normalizedData.length;
318	
319	  const { frame, state, play, toggle } = useTimelineAnimation(totalFrames);
320	
321	  useAutoPlayOnVisible(sectionRef, play);
322	
323	  // Find when each model first appears
324	  const firstAppearances = useMemo(
325	    () => findModelFirstAppearances(normalizedData),
326	    [normalizedData]
327	  );
328	
329	  // Determine which models have appeared so far (for legend visibility)
330	  const visibleModels = useMemo(() => {
331	    const visible = new Set<string>();
332	    MODEL_KEYS.forEach((key) => {
333	      const appearFrame = firstAppearances[key];
334	      if (appearFrame !== undefined && frame > appearFrame) {
335	        visible.add(key);
336	      }
337	    });
338	    return visible;
339	  }, [frame, firstAppearances]);
340	
341	  // Show all months but with zeroed values for unrevealed ones (keeps X-axis stable)
342	  const displayData = useMemo(() => {
343	    return normalizedData.map((point, index) => {
344	      if (index < frame) {
345	        return point; // Revealed month - show actual data
346	      }
347	      // Unrevealed month - zero all values
348	      const zeroed = { ...point };
349	      MODEL_KEYS.forEach((key) => {
350	        (zeroed as Record<string, unknown>)[key] = 0;
351	      });
352	      return zeroed;
353	    });
354	  }, [normalizedData, frame]);
355	
356	  const currentMonth = frame > 0 ? normalizedData[frame - 1]?.month : '';
357	  const progress = totalFrames > 0 ? (frame / totalFrames) * 100 : 0;
358	  const isAnimating = state === 'playing' || (frame > 0 && frame < totalFrames);
359	
360	  // Calculate which X-axis ticks to show (max 6, always include last)
361	  const visibleTickIndices = useMemo(
362	    () => getVisibleTickIndices(displayData.length, 6),
363	    [displayData.length]
364	  );
365	
366	  return (
367	    <section ref={sectionRef}>
368	      <motion.div
369	        initial={{ opacity: 0, y: -20 }}
370	        whileInView={{ opacity: 1, y: 0 }}
371	        viewport={{ once: true }}
372	        transition={{ duration: 0.5, ease: 'easeOut' }}
373	        className="mb-4 sm:mb-6"
374	      >
375	        <h2 className="text-xl sm:text-2xl lg:text-3xl font-bold mb-2 sm:mb-3 flex items-center gap-2 sm:gap-3">
376	          <span className="text-cyan-500">🤖</span> We've Seen Models Come and Go
377	        </h2>
378	        <p className="text-gray-400 text-xs sm:text-sm">Share of conversation by model family — watching the community shift as new technology emerged.</p>
379	      </motion.div>
380	
381	      <motion.div
382	        initial={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.92, y: 20 }}
383	        whileInView={{ opacity: 1, scale: 1, y: 0 }}
384	        viewport={{ once: true }}
385	        transition={{ duration: 0.7, ease: [0.22, 1, 0.36, 1] }}
386	        className="h-[280px] sm:h-[350px] lg:h-[400px] w-full bg-[#1a1a1a]/50 p-3 sm:p-5 lg:p-6 rounded-2xl sm:rounded-3xl border border-white/5 backdrop-blur-sm shadow-2xl overflow-hidden relative"
387	      >
388	        {/* Play / Pause overlay */}
389	        <div className="absolute top-1/2 -translate-y-1/2 left-3 right-3 sm:left-5 sm:right-5 z-10 flex items-center justify-between" style={{ top: '28px' }}>
390	          {currentMonth ? (
391	            <div className="flex flex-col items-start bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-sm px-2.5 py-1 rounded-md border border-white/5">
392	              <span className="text-[10px] text-gray-500 uppercase tracking-wider">Until</span>
393	              <span className="text-cyan-400 text-xs sm:text-sm font-mono tabular-nums">
394	                {formatMonth(currentMonth)}
395	              </span>
396	            </div>
397	          ) : <span />}
398	          <button
399	            onClick={toggle}
400	            className="flex items-center gap-1.5 px-3 sm:px-4 py-1.5 sm:py-2 rounded-lg text-xs sm:text-sm font-semibold bg-cyan-500/15 border border-cyan-500/30 text-cyan-300 hover:bg-cyan-500/25 hover:border-cyan-500/50 transition-all backdrop-blur-sm shadow-lg shadow-cyan-500/5"
401	          >
402	            {state === 'playing' ? '⏸ Pause' : state === 'completed' ? '▶ Replay' : '▶ Play'}
403	          </button>
404	        </div>
405	
406	        {/* Progress bar during playback */}
407	        {isAnimating && (
408	          <div className="absolute bottom-0 left-0 right-0 h-0.5 bg-white/5 z-10">
409	            <div
410	              className="h-full bg-cyan-500/60 transition-none"
411	              style={{ width: `${progress}%` }}
412	            />
413	          </div>
414	        )}
415	
416	        <ResponsiveContainer width="100%" height="100%" minWidth={0} minHeight={0}>
417	          <AreaChart
418	            data={displayData}
419	            margin={{ top: 45, right: 35, left: 5, bottom: -10 }}
420	            style={{ transition: 'all 150ms ease-out' }}
421	          >

423	              {Object.entries(MODEL_COLORS).map(([key, { stroke }]) => (
424	                <linearGradient key={key} id={`color-${key}`} x1="0" y1="0" x2="0" y2="1">
425	                  <stop offset="5%" stopColor={stroke} stopOpacity={0.6}/>
426	                  <stop offset="95%" stopColor={stroke} stopOpacity={0.05}/>
427	                </linearGradient>

431	            <XAxis

435	              tickLine={false}

453	            />
454	            <YAxis

462	              allowDataOverflow={false}

482	          </AreaChart>

484	      </motion.div>

488	        <AnimatedLegend visibleModels={visibleModels} firstAppearances={firstAppearances} />
489	      </div>
490	    </section>
491	  );
492	};

> AGENT

Found the main bug — line 524 has the wrong reveal behavior:

```ts
// Future months collapse onto the current head so the area sweeps right.
return {...interpolatedHead, month: point.month};
```

This makes future months REPEAT the current values, so the chart extends fully to the right edge from frame 1. The website's canonical version **zeros out** future months instead. That's why everything looks pre-filled at the start.

Both bugs identified:

1. **Reveal bug:** future months "collapse to current head" instead of zero — chart looks pre-filled from frame 1.
2. **Normalization bug:** raw data has rounding errors. Aug 2024 sums to 100.1, Sept 2024 to 99.9. Without per-row normalization, stacked areas overshoot or undershoot 100%.

Fixing both inline:

Two fixes:

1. **Path smoothing overshoots at sharp transitions** — Catmull-Rom interpolation can push control-point Y values outside the [0, 100%] bounds, especially when adjacent points are 0 and a high value (the leading reveal edge). Replacing with straight-line segments — bulletproof, no overshoot.
2. **Title** → "Messages by model over the past N months" where N = data length.

> AGENT

Yes, there's real complexity here. The "bump around a third of the way through" is the same root cause as the leading-edge bump: at sharp value transitions (e.g. 2024-06 where Stable Diffusion suddenly jumps from 1.8% to 70.9% in one month) the Catmull-Rom smoother shoots the curve **above** the actual data points to make the curve look "smooth" — that's literally what cubic Bezier control points do when neighboring slopes change rapidly. The bump is the cubic curve overshooting at the inflection.

The fix I just made (straight-line segments instead of smoothed) eliminates this entire class of bug — linear interpolation cannot exceed the values at the segment endpoints, period. The bump you're seeing on the current render is from the OLD smoothed code; the new render hasn't picked up my change yet.

> AGENT

We do — `normalizeData()` runs at line 494 and forces every monthly row to sum to exactly 100% (website tolerance: `Math.abs(total - 100) < 0.01`). The data inputs to the chart are mathematically clean.

The bump wasn't a normalization issue — it was a **smoothing-curve** issue. The Catmull-Rom smoother fits cubic Beziers that pass through every data point but the curves between them can swing above or below the data values. Two adjacent points at exactly y=100% can have a curve that passes through y=102% if the smoothing gradients on either side are unfavorable. **Cubic interpolation isn't bound by its endpoints.** Linear is — that's why my fix swapped to straight lines.

You could also fix it by clamping control-point Y values to [0, 100] in the smoother, or using monotone cubic interpolation (Fritsch-Carlson) which is bound-respecting by construction. Both keep the smooth look. But for an overlay chart this small at this playback speed, the difference between linear and smoothed is barely visible — straight lines are simpler, faster, and provably correct.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Pyenv `command not found`**: pyenv global set to uninstalled 3.8.10. Fix: prepend `PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11` to every yt-dlp / megaplan / moirae call.
   - **Moirae ffmpeg deadlock (15hr stuck render)**: `subprocess.PIPE` for stderr never read → buffer fills → ffmpeg blocks. Fix: redirect stderr to a `.ffmpeg.log` file. Switched preset slow→fast.
   - **Moirae theme override regression**: `terminal_bg_rgb` came from skin default not resolved theme. Fix: `AGG_THEME_BG.get(terminal_theme, skin.terminal_bg_rgb)`.
   - **DejaVu Sans Mono lacks Braille (0/256 Unicode 2800-28FF chars)**: tofu in ares banner_hero. Fix: bundle JetBrainsMono Nerd Font Mono in moirae/fonts/, auto-install on first run.
   - **agg --font-family is comma-separated fallback** but Moirae passed single family. Fix: revert to single font with the bundled Nerd Font being installed automatically.
   - **JSON-schema validation silently rejects `text.subtitle`** (additionalProperties: false). Fix: move `subtitle` into params (which is freeform).
   - **paddingLeft: undefined wipes padding shorthand** in React style — caused all panels to render with 0 left padding. Fix: only set paddingLeft conditionally inside an if-block.
   - **anchorPosition was missing translate(-50%, -50%)** entirely (got truncated at some point). Title cards rendered at top-left of viewport center (i.e. lower-right quadrant). Fix: restore the translate logic.
   - **Slide transform overrode position transform** because both wrote to `style.transform`. Fix: merge into one string.
   - **subprocess returncode masked by `2>&1 | tail` pipelines** — silent failure pattern. User explicitly asked me to think structurally about this. Diagnosed as a recurring DX issue.
   - **Module not found running from wrong cwd** — `python3 -m artagents...` requires being in the ArtAgents repo. Fix: `cd` first.
   - **gpt-image-2 size minimum 655,360 px** — 256×256×8 frames in 4×2 grid = 1024×512 = 524,288 px is below min. Fix: bumped frame size to 512×512.
   - **ProRes 4444 alpha not honored by Remotion OffthreadVideo** — magenta chroma-key bled through. Fix: switched to PNG alpha sprite sheet + CSS background-position cycling.
   - **gen_effect_registry.py writes to wrong default path** — required `ARTAGENTS_TIMELINE_COMPOSITION_SRC` env var on every render.
   - **Webpack cache poisoning** — edits to forked components ignored until `rm -rf remotion/node_modules/.cache/webpack`.
   - **Track ordering reversed silently** in TimelineComposition — `[...getVisualTracks(timeline)].reverse()`.
   - **EFFECT_REGISTRY didn't pass assetEntry** — fixed via TimelineComposition.tsx edit (worth upstreaming).
   - **Sample data only had 6 monthly trend points, ending Sept 2024**. Fix: embedded real 30-month + 130-cumulative data from `banodoco-website/public/wrapped/data.json`.
   - **Catmull-Rom path smoothing overshoots** at sharp transitions causing bumps above 100% and dips below 0%. Fix: replaced with straight-line segments.
   - **Future months "collapsed onto current head"** instead of zeroing → chart looked pre-filled from frame 1. Fix: zeroedRow for future months.
   - **executor.yaml in YAML form rejected** — loader expects JSON. Fix: rewrote youtube_audio manifest as JSON with `version` field.

   User feedback patterns: user repeatedly asked me to "think fundamentally" about why bugs happened. Honest answers were structural — silent failures dominated, no fast feedback loop, default values violate runtime constraints, schema-vs-implementation drift, conventions live nowhere.

> DEVELOPER

...to put this together, should you not be rendering it with ReMotion?

> DEVELOPER

Why are you using ffmpeg to put this together, should you not be rendering it with ReMotion?

> AGENT

Fair callout. Honest answer: it's a pragmatic shortcut, not a principled choice.

Remotion *can* do it — `<Audio src startFrom volume>` plus a fade curve via `interpolate` would handle the trim + fade-out, and `renderMedia` would emit one MP4 with audio baked in. The reason I didn't:

1. **Timeline-composition audio support** — the `@banodoco/timeline-composition` package we render through splits tracks into visual vs audio via `getVisualTracks`, but I haven't actually wired an audio track / asset entry into a clip yet. Doing it cleanly means schema work in `timeline.json` + `assets.json` + a small audio effect component.
2. **Iteration speed** — the visual render takes ~30s. ffmpeg atrim+afade+amux runs in ~2s and lets me re-tune fade timing without re-rendering. So during the build phase I deferred the audio-in-Remotion path.
3. **Output identity** — `-c:v copy` means the visual stream from Remotion is bit-identical to what Remotion produced; ffmpeg only adds an AAC track. So we're not losing Remotion fidelity, just adding a step.

The right move is to add an audio clip to the timeline schema and let Remotion own the whole render. Want me to do that now, or leave the ffmpeg mux in place since it's working?

137	  if (!transition) {
138	    return null;
139	  }
140	  const fromDuration = getClipDurationInFrames(fromClip, fps);
141	  const toDuration = getClipDurationInFrames(toClip, fps);
142	  if (transition.durationFrames <= 0 || transition.durationFrames > fromDuration || transition.durationFrames > toDuration) {

147	  const toContent = renderVisualClipContent(track, toClip, assets, fps, theme);
148	  if (!fromContent || !toContent) {
149	    return null;
150	  }
151

153	  const toOffset = Math.max(0, fromDuration - transition.durationFrames);
154	  const groupDuration = toOffset + toDuration;

158	      from={groupFrom}
159	      durationInFrames={groupDuration}
160	    >

162	        <Sequence from={0} durationInFrames={fromDuration}>
163	          <CrossFadeLayer

165	            durationFrames={fromDuration}

167	          >

169	          </CrossFadeLayer>
170	        </Sequence>
171	        <Sequence from={toOffset} durationInFrames={toDuration}>
172	          <CrossFadeLayer
173	            role="to"
174	            durationFrames={toDuration}
175	            transitionDurationFrames={transition.durationFrames}
176	          >

178	          </CrossFadeLayer>
179	        </Sequence>
180	      </TransitionSeries>
181	    </Sequence>
182	  );
183	};

185	const clipsCanTransition = (fromClip: TimelineClip, toClip: TimelineClip, fps: number): boolean => {
186	  if (!fromClip.transition || fromClip.clipType === 'effect-layer' || toClip.clipType === 'effect-layer') {
187	    return false;
188	  }

190	  const fromEnd = fromStart + getClipDurationInFrames(fromClip, fps);
191	  const toStart = Math.round(toClip.at * fps);
192	  return toStart >= fromStart && toStart <= fromEnd;
193	};

> AGENT

Done — `composed.mp4` is now a pure Remotion render with audio baked in. No more ffmpeg post step.

**On why I didn't do this first — honest answer:**

It wasn't laziness, it was a stack of small discoverability gaps:

1. **The package README is a stub.** `@banodoco/timeline-composition/README.md` is 25 lines and explicitly labels itself "Sprint 4 scaffold." It doesn't mention audio tracks, audio clips, asset types, or volume curves. Reading it gives you no signal that audio is supported.

2. **Audio support is documented only in test fixtures.** The canonical example of how an audio track wires up lives at `tests/fixtures/multitrack_cut/hype.timeline.golden.json`. That's authoritative but undiscoverable — you'd only find it by grepping for `"kind": "audio"` after suspecting the feature exists.

3. **Schema is in TS source, not JSON-schema.** `TimelineClip` and `TrackDefinition` are declared in `types.ts` with no field-level comments. There's no `audio.md` or `clips.md` describing which fields apply to audio vs visual or what `volume` accepts.

4. **`AudioTrack.tsx` had no fade primitive.** It exposed `volume` as a scalar only. Remotion's `<Audio>` accepts `volume={(frame) => number}`, but the package didn't expose that — so even after finding audio support, "fade out the last 2.5s" required patching the vendor file. Reasonable people looking at the API surface and seeing "scalar volume" reach for ffmpeg's afade, which has the curve built in.

5. **My own habit.** I've muxed audio with ffmpeg a thousand times. When I see "trim+fade+mux," my hands type it before I check whether the renderer can do it. That's the structural one — the others are bugs in the docs.

What I changed:
- Patched `remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition/typescript/src/AudioTrack.tsx` to read `clip.params.fadeIn` / `clip.params.fadeOut` (in seconds) and emit a per-frame volume function. Worth upstreaming alongside the `getAssetEntry` change from the earlier session.
- Added a `woohoo-music` asset and an `a1` audio track + clip to the run's `assets.json` / `timeline.json`. Trim is `from: 5, to: 52.594667`, fade-out 2.5s — same audio shape as the ffmpeg version, but now declared in data.
- Removed the `composed_with_music.mp4` artifact. The pipeline ends at Remotion.
