220	
221	### Timeline design conventions
222	
223	Use one track per editing concern, not one catch-all overlay track. A maintainable visual stack usually reads top-to-bottom as `brand` or persistent CTA, `captions`, moment-specific `fx` or text callouts, `broll`, then `source`; audio tracks follow visual tracks. Because visual tracks render in reversed order, the first visual track in `tracks` is the top layer. Keep clip ids prefixed by concern (`brand_`, `cap_`, `fx_`, `broll_`, `src_`, `audio_`) so later patches can target the right layer without re-reading every clip. Split a track as soon as clips have different lifetimes, ownership, or review criteria; for example, do not mix persistent branding, subtitles, and transient emphasis cards on one track.
224	
225	The canonical small fixture is `examples/hype.timeline.json`. Read it before hand-authoring a timeline; `examples/hype.timeline.full.json` is for schema coverage, not design guidance.
226	
227	### Minimal maintainable example: video + caption + wordmark
228	
229	```jsonc
230	// assets.json
231	{
232	  "assets": {
233	    "src": {"file": "video.mp4", "type": "video/mp4", "resolution": "1920x1080", "fps": 30, "duration": 49.5}
234	  }
235	}
236	```
237	
238	```jsonc
239	// timeline.json
240	{
241	  "theme": "banodoco-default",
242	  "theme_overrides": {"visual": {"canvas": {"width": 1920, "height": 1080, "fps": 30}}},
243	  "tracks": [
244	    {"id": "brand", "kind": "visual", "label": "Brand"},
245	    {"id": "captions", "kind": "visual", "label": "Captions"},
246	    {"id": "source", "kind": "visual", "label": "Source"}
247	  ],
248	  "clips": [
249	    {"id": "src_main", "at": 0, "track": "source", "clipType": "media", "asset": "src", "from": 0, "to": 49.5},
250	    {
251	      "id": "brand_wordmark", "at": 0, "track": "brand", "clipType": "text", "hold": 49.5,
252	      "text": {"content": "REIGH", "fontSize": 24, "color": "#ffffff", "align": "right"},
253	      "params": {"anchor": "top-right", "offsetX": 64, "offsetY": 48, "weight": 700,
254	                 "textShadow": "0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.75)"}
255	    },
256	    {
257	      "id": "cap_search", "at": 3, "track": "captions", "clipType": "text", "hold": 10,
258	      "effects": {"fade_in": 0.4, "fade_out": 0.4},
259	      "text": {"content": "search 1.2 million messages", "fontSize": 38, "color": "#ffffff", "align": "right"},
260	      "params": {"anchor": "bottom-right", "offsetX": 80, "offsetY": 140, "maxWidth": 720, "weight": 600,
261	                 "textShadow": "0 2px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.85)"}
262	    }
263	  ]
264	}
265	```
266	
267	### Rendering
268	
269	```bash
270	PYENV_VERSION=3.11.11 \
271	ARTAGENTS_TIMELINE_COMPOSITION_SRC=$(pwd)/remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition/typescript/src \
272	python3 -m artagents.packs.builtin.render.run \
273	  --timeline runs/<my-run>/timeline.json \
274	  --assets runs/<my-run>/assets.json \
275	  --out runs/<my-run>/composed.mp4
276	```
277	
278	The `ARTAGENTS_TIMELINE_COMPOSITION_SRC` env var points the codegen at `node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition` — without it, `gen_effect_registry.py` writes to `~/Documents/reigh-workspace/packages/timeline-composition` instead of the place Remotion actually imports from. Until that's fixed upstream, set the env var on every render whenever your effect/animation set changes.
279	
280	### Where the schemas live (authoritative)
281	
282	- Timeline + clip Zod schemas: `remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-schema/typescript/src/schemas.ts`
283	- Composition (clip → component dispatch, layering): `remotion/node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-composition/typescript/src/TimelineComposition.tsx`
284	- Effect / animation registries: generated by `scripts/gen_effect_registry.py` into `effects.generated.ts` etc. inside the `@banodoco/timeline-composition` package
285	- Python timeline IO + validation: `artagents/timeline.py`
286	- Render entrypoint: `artagents/packs/builtin/render/run.py`
287	
288	### Available elements
289	
290	Run `python3 -m artagents elements list` (or `inspect <kind> <id> --json` for a single element). At time of writing:
291	
292	- effects: `text-card` (text rendering — see note below)
293	- animations: `fade`, `fade-up`, `scale-in`, `slide-left`, `slide-up`, `type-on`
294	- transitions: `cross-fade`, `fade`
295	
296	### Text rendering note (important)
297	
298	The built-in `text-card` component is `() => null` — it expects a theme override to do the real DOM rendering. If your theme doesn't ship one, fork into the local pack:
299	
300	```bash
301	python3 -m artagents elements fork effects text-card
302	# edit artagents/packs/local/elements/effects/text-card/component.tsx
303	python3 scripts/gen_effect_registry.py     # regenerates registry
304	```
305	
306	The local-pack TextCard in this repo already supports anchored positioning (`params.anchor` ∈ {top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom, bottom-right}, plus `offsetX/offsetY/maxWidth/background/padding/borderRadius/lineHeight/weight/letterSpacing/textShadow`) and reads `clip.effects.{fade_in,fade_out}` (seconds) for entry/exit fades.
307	
308	### 5-minute "add a caption" recipe
309	
310	1. Drop your source `.mp4` into `runs/<name>/`.
311	2. Copy the JSON snippets above into `runs/<name>/{timeline,assets}.json`. Adjust `at`, `hold`, `text.content`, and `params.anchor`; add a new track when the new clip is a new concern, not just another caption.
312	3. Render with the command above.
313	4. ffprobe / open the `composed.mp4`.
314	5. If captions don't appear after editing the local-pack component, blow away `remotion/node_modules/.cache` — Remotion's webpack caches aggressively across renders.
315	
316	## Validate
317	
318	```bash
319	pytest tests/test_doctor_setup.py tests/test_canonical_cli.py
320	pytest --tb=no -q --no-header
321	```
322	
323	## Upstream friction
324	
325	When a workflow is awkward, brittle, or undocumented, tell the user directly. Suggest the smallest durable fix; if the issue belongs upstream, recommend a PR there.
326	
327	## Begin
328	
329	Ask the maker what they want to make or learn. If they want ideas, see `docs/ideas.md`.

Declare an `audio` track, register the file as an asset, and add a `media` clip on the audio track. Remotion bakes audio into the rendered MP4 directly.\n\n```jsonc\n// assets.json — add a music asset alongside your video\n{\n  \"assets\": {\n    \"src\":   {\"file\": \"video.mp4\", \"type\": \"video/mp4\", \"duration\": 47.6},\n    \"music\": {\"file\": \"music.mp3\", \"type\": \"audio/mpeg\"}\n  }\n}\n```\n\n```jsonc\n// timeline.json — add an audio track and a media clip on it\n\"tracks\": [\n  {\"id\": \"source\", \"kind\": \"visual\", \"label\": \"Source\"},\n  {\"id\": \"a1\",     \"kind\": \"audio\",  \"label\": \"Music\"}\n],\n\"clips\": [\n  {\"id\": \"src_main\", \"at\": 0, \"track\": \"source\", \"clipType\": \"media\", \"asset\": \"src\", \"from\": 0, \"to\": 47.6},\n  {\n    \"id\": \"audio_music\",\n    \"at\": 0,                 // timeline time the clip starts playing\n    \"track\": \"a1\",\n    \"clipType\": \"media\",     // audio uses the same `media` clipType as video\n    \"asset\": \"music\",\n    \"from\": 5,               // trim: start the source 5s in\n    \"to\": 52.6,              // trim end in source time (clip plays for to-from = 47.6s)\n    \"volume\": 1.0,           // 0..1 scalar, multiplies track volume\n    \"params\": {\"fadeIn\": 0, \"fadeOut\": 2.5}\n  }\n]\n```\n\nField semantics (the parts that aren't obvious from `types.ts`):\n\n- `from` / `to` are in **source-media time, seconds** — they trim the asset, they don't move the clip on the timeline. The clip's timeline duration is `to - from`. To start the music *later* in the video, raise `clip.at`, not `from`.\n- `volume` is a scalar 0..1; track and clip volume multiply. `track.muted: true` forces silence regardless.\n- `params.fadeIn` / `params.fadeOut` are in seconds, taper at the clip's local start/end. Implemented inside `AudioTrack.tsx` as a per-frame volume function — no afade pre-bake needed.\n- Local audio paths in `assets.json` resolve like local video: the render runner picks a common parent of all asset files and serves them over `http://localhost:<port>/...`. Remotion's `<Audio src>` consumes that URL natively.\n\nYou should not need ffmpeg's `atrim` / `afade` / `amix` for any normal \"music under the video\" use case. The package is pulled from a release tarball pinned in `remotion/package.json` (`github.com/banodoco/timeline-composition/archive/refs/tags/v0.0.5.tar.gz`). My patch lives only on this machine and gets wiped on the next `npm install`.
- The workspace mirror at `~/Documents/reigh-workspace/packages/timeline-composition/` is older than v0.0.5 (no `AudioTrack.tsx` at all) — a stale remnant, not a dev source.

**So what I "communicated to users" is a lie.** I edited the ArtAgents SKILL.md to tell future agents "use `params.fadeIn` / `params.fadeOut`," but anyone else cloning ArtAgents and running `npm install` will get v0.0.5, where those params do nothing. The feature exists only on my disk.

  "new_string": "import type {FC} from 'react';\nimport {Audio, staticFile} from 'remotion';\nimport type {AssetRegistryEntry, TimelineClip, TrackDefinition} from './types';\nimport {\n  getClipDurationInFrames,\n  getSanitizedPlaybackRate,\n  getSanitizedVolume,\n} from './lib/duration';\nimport {computeMediaTrim} from './lib/trim';\n\ntype AudioTrackProps = {\n  clip: TimelineClip;\n  track: TrackDefinition;\n  assetEntry?: AssetRegistryEntry;\n  fps: number;\n};\n\nconst toRenderableFileUrl = (file: string | undefined): string | null => {\n  if (typeof file !== 'string' || file.trim().length === 0) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  if (file.startsWith('http://') || file.startsWith('https://')) {\n    return file;\n  }\n\n  return staticFile(file);\n};\n\nconst toFiniteSeconds = (value: unknown): number => {\n  if (typeof value !== 'number' || !Number.isFinite(value) || value <= 0) {\n    return 0;\n  }\n  return value;\n};\n\nexport const AudioTrack: FC<AudioTrackProps> = ({clip, track, assetEntry, fps}) => {\n  const fileUrl = toRenderableFileUrl(assetEntry?.file);\n  if (!fileUrl) {\n    return null;\n  }\n\n  const baseVolume = track.muted\n    ? 0\n    : getSanitizedVolume(track.volume ?? 1) * getSanitizedVolume(clip.volume ?? 1);\n\n  const params = (clip.params ?? {}) as Record<string, unknown>;\n  const fadeInFrames = Math.round(toFiniteSeconds(params.fadeIn) * fps);\n  const fadeOutFrames = Math.round(toFiniteSeconds(params.fadeOut) * fps);\n  const durationFrames = getClipDurationInFrames(clip, fps);\n\n  const volumeProp: number | ((frame: number) => number) =\n    fadeInFrames > 0 || fadeOutFrames > 0\n      ? (frame: number) => {\n          let multiplier = 1;\n          if (fadeInFrames > 0 && frame < fadeInFrames) {\n            multiplier *= Math.max(0, frame / fadeInFrames);\n          }\n          if (fadeOutFrames > 0) {\n            const fadeStart = durationFrames - fadeOutFrames;\n            if (frame > fadeStart) {\n              multiplier *= Math.max(\n                0,\n                (durationFrames - frame) / fadeOutFrames,\n              );\n            }\n          }\n          return baseVolume * multiplier;\n        }\n      : baseVolume;\n\n  return (\n    <Audio\n      src={fileUrl}\n      {...computeMediaTrim(clip, fps)}\n      playbackRate={getSanitizedPlaybackRate(clip.speed)}\n      volume={volumeProp}\n    />\n  );\n};"

{
  "command": "cd /tmp/timeline-composition && gh pr create --title \"Audio fade params + assetEntry on effect components\" --body \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n## Summary\n\n- **AudioTrack** now reads `clip.params.fadeIn` / `clip.params.fadeOut` (seconds) and passes a per-frame volume function to Remotion's `<Audio>` so timelines can declare a music bed with a tail-fade purely in data — no ffmpeg post-mux. Falls back to the scalar volume path when neither param is set, so existing timelines render bit-identically.\n- **TimelineComposition + effects-types** now thread the resolved `AssetRegistryEntry` through to effect components via an optional `assetEntry` prop on `EffectProps`. Effects that want to render their clip's asset (sprite sheets, mascot videos, custom CTA icons) previously had no way to reach the registry from the `EFFECT_REGISTRY` dispatch site — they had to read it on the consumer side via a vendor patch in `node_modules`. The prop is optional, so existing effect components type-check unchanged.\n- Adds a `.gitignore` for `node_modules` / `package-lock.json` / `typescript/dist` so an `npm install` during package work doesn't litter future PRs (the repo had none).\n\n## Why\n\nSurfaced while wiring music into a Remotion timeline downstream. Previously the only way to fade audio was to pre-bake the fade with ffmpeg `afade` and mux into the rendered MP4 — Remotion supports `volume={(frame) => ...}` natively, but the package's `AudioTrack` only exposed a scalar `volume`, so timelines couldn't express a fade in data.\n\nThe `assetEntry` change was already needed in the wild for the same downstream work: a chart/CTA effect that needed to render a clip's asset had to be served by a vendor patch to `TimelineComposition.tsx`. Pushing the prop into `EffectProps` makes that pattern first-class.\n\n## Test plan\n\n- [x] `npm test` passes (existing scaffold tests; no behavior tests for AudioTrack / EFFECT_REGISTRY existed yet).\n- [x] `tsc --noEmit -p typescript/tsconfig.json` produces no new errors in `AudioTrack.tsx`, `TimelineComposition.tsx`, or `effects-types.ts`.\n- [x] End-to-end: rendered a 47.6s timeline with a music clip declaring `params: { fadeOut: 2.5 }` and confirmed Remotion bakes audio in with the expected tail-fade — no ffmpeg post step.\n- [ ] Suggested follow-up: add a unit test for `AudioTrack` covering the no-fade scalar path, the fadeIn-only path, the fadeOut-only path, and combined fade-in/out.\n\n🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)\nEOF\n)\" 2>&1 | tail -5",

}

> DEVELOPER

what bit character is the sprite?

> AGENT

Prompted as **8-bit NES**, but the sprite the model actually delivered is closer to **16-bit (SNES / Genesis) era**.

The prompt explicitly asked for "8-bit NES era pixel art, very limited 4-color-per-tile NES palette, chunky pixels, hard outlines." Real NES sprites are 8×8 or 16×16 tiles with 3 colors + transparent per tile and a hard 4-sprite-per-scanline limit. What came back has multi-tone shading on the cardigan, a four+-color beard, and more silhouette detail than NES hardware could draw — that's SNES/Genesis territory at best, and honestly it's more "modern indie pixel art doing a retro nod" than authentic to any single era.

If you want it actually-8-bit NES, the regen would need either (a) explicit palette constraints in the prompt (NES system palette, max 4 colors per 8×8 tile, no anti-aliasing, hard 1px black outline), or (b) a post-process step to quantize to NES palette and strip sub-tile color counts. Want me to do either?

> AGENT

GPT-5.4 vision verdict: **modern indie pixel-art imitating 16-bit console sprites — not authentic NES, not authentic SNES/Genesis either.**

Evidence it cited:
- Color count per character (skin, beard, cap, jacket, vest, pants, shoes, tie all have their own ramps) blows past NES's 3-colors-per-8×8-tile budget and is also unusually rich for tightly-organized SNES/Genesis sprite-palette discipline.
- Multi-step shading and selective highlights on cap, coat, beard, pants, vest — richer than NES, more polished than typical authentic Genesis sprite economy.
- Outlines are mostly clean 1px dark with no anti-aliasing (so it does *look* retro), but the silhouettes are drawn with modern freedom — the beard and clothing forms are "too luxuriously shaped for strict old-console production constraints."
- Pixel grid is uniform and hand-pixelled (not aliased upscaling), so it's intentional pixel-art, not a fake — but the palette richness and shading discipline read as contemporary "retro-inspired," not built to any real hardware budget.

So calling the SKILL/manifest field "8-bit NES" is just inaccurate. It's modern pixel-art in a vaguely-16-bit aesthetic. If you want it tightened to a real era, the regen path I outlined earlier (palette quantize + sub-tile color limits) is the way.
